उपधारा (4) के अधीन जारी की गई भारत सरकार के पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का. 
a. (35 तारीख 27 जनवरी, 2025, जो भारत के साप्ताहिक राजपत्र तारीख जनवरी 26, --फरवरी — 2025, में 
प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा उस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में आन्ध्र प्रदेश राज्य में पैट्रोलियम 
पदार्थ परिवाहन के लिए हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड द्वारा विसाख (आन्ध्र प्रदेश) से रायपुर (छत्तीसगढ) 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के प्रयोजन के लिए उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी;

और उक्त साप्ताहिक राजपत्र अधिसूचना की प्रतियां जनता को तारीख 28 अप्रैल, 2025 को उपलब्ध करा दी 
गई थी ; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा () के अधीन केन्द्रीय सरकार को रिपोर्ट दे 
दी है; 


और केन्द्रीय सरकार ने, उक्त रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के पश्चात, और यह समाधान हो जाने पर कि उक्त भूमि 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए अपेक्षित है, उसमें उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने का विनिश्चय किया है ; 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा (॥) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते 
हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि इस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए 
उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन किया जाए ; 

और केन्द्रीय सरकार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उपधारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह 
निर्देश देती है कि उक्त भूमि में उपयोग का अधिकार इस घोषणा के प्रकाशन की तारीख से केन्द्रीय सरकार में निहित 
होने के बजाए, सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त होकर हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड में निहित होगा। 

पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन अधिनियम, 962 की धारा 40 के अधीन किसी भी क्षतिपूर्ति के लिए 
हिन्दुस्तान पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड पूर्णतया उत्तरदायी होगी और धारा 43 के अधीन पाइपलाइन से सम्बन्धित 
किसी भी मामले पर केन्द्रीय सरकार के विरूद्ध कोई वाद, दावा या कानूनी कार्यवाही नहीं हो सकेगी ;

MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
New Delhi, the |lth August, 2025 


S.O. 469.—Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas, number S.O. 35(E) dated the 27th January, 2025, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the 
Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962) (hereinafter 
referred to as “the said Act’), and published in the Weekly Gazette of India dated January 26 — February |, 2025, 
the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the Right of User in the land specified in the Schedule 
appended to that notification, for the purpose of laying a pipeline for transportation of petroleum products from 
Visakha (Andhra Pradesh) to Raipur (Chhattisgarh) in the State of Andhra Pradesh by Hindustan Petroleum 
Corporation Limited; 


And whereas copies of the said Weekly Gazette notification were made available to the public on 28th 
April, 2025; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has, under sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act, submitted 
his report to the Central Government; 


And whereas the Central Government, after considering the said report and being satisfied that the said 
land is required for the purpose of laying the said pipeline, has decided to acquire the Right of User therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act, the 
Central Government hereby declares that the Right of User in the land specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification is acquired for the purpose of laying the said pipeline; 


And further, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 6 of the said Act, the 
Central Government hereby directs that the Right of User in the said land for laying the pipeline shall, instead of 
vesting in the Central Government, vest on the date of publication of this declaration, in Hindustan Petroleum 
Corporation Limited, free from all encumbrances; 


Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited shall be exclusively liable for any compensation in terms of 
Section l0 of the said Act; 


Further, in accordance with Section [3 of the said Act, no suit, claim, or legal proceeding shall lie against the 
Central Government in respect of any matter relating to the said pipeline.

AWARD. 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub —section (2A) of Section 0 
of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947),Government Of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
Order No.L-2002/44/2000-IR(C-I) dated 29/05/2003 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between 
the employer i.e. management of Bastacolla Area of M/s. BCCL and their workman through Central Secretary, 
Bihar Colliery Kamgar Union, Dhanbad for adjudication by this Tribunal: 


“क्या बिहार कोलियरी कामगार यूनियन की भारत कोकिंग कोल लिमिटेड, बस्ताकोला क्षेत्र के प्रबंधतंत्र 


से माँग कि श्री Tag पासवान एवं सूची में दिए गए अन्य 75 कर्मकारों को नियमित किया जाये उचित 
एवं न्‍्यायसंगत है? यदि हाँ तो कर्मकार किस राहत के पात्र हैं तथा किस तारीख से?”

2. On receiving order no. L-2002/44/2000-IR(C-I) dated 29/05/2003 Government of India, Ministry of 
Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, Reference case no. 45 of 2003 was registered on !6.06.2003 
and thereafter the notices were sent to the parties with a direction to appear and submit their written statements 
along with relevant documents in support of their claims and the witnesses. 


3. After issuance of regd. notice, written statement has been filed by Sri K. Chakraborty, Ld. Advocate on behalf 
of the workmen. Sri U.N. Lal, Ld. Advocate appeared from the side of the management and filed his letter of 
authority on 28.08.2003. It further transpires that written statement cum rejoinder has been filed by the 
management but when the case record was put up after a long gap, registered notices were again sent but the 
registered post was returned with remarks “अधूरा पता वापस and thereafter no step was taken from the side of the 
workmen. Though on 3.06.2025, Sri N. Nath, O.S Legal (HQ) appeared from the side of the management but the 
workmen never appeared before the Tribunal since 3.02.2006. 


4. On perusal of the entire case record it is transpires that the workmen never appeared before this Tribunal for 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5677 


a period of 9 years which shows that the workmen have lost their interest in this case and therefore, for the ends 
of justice, this case deserves to be dismissed for non prosecution. 


5. Hence, 
ORDERED 


that this case is hereby dismissed and a “No Dispute Award” be drawn up in respect of the above reference case. 
Let the copies of Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, 
New Delhi for information and notification. 


SACHINDRA KUMAR PANDEY, Presiding Officer

AWARD 


The Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-2202/26/20I5— IR(CM.ID) 
dated 8.6.20I5 referred the following dispute under section 0(l)(d) of the I.D. Act, !947 for adjudication to this 
Tribunal between the management of M/s. Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., and their workman.The reference 
is, 


“Whether the action of the General Manager, M/s. Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., Bellampalli Area, 
Goleti Township (P.O.), Adilabad Distt., in terminating the services of Sri Jellala Balaiah, Ex-Badli 
Filler, Goleti-l Inc, SCCo. Ltd., Bellampalli Area with effect from 9.5.2008 is justified or not? If not, to 
what relief the applicant is entitled for?” 


The reference is numbered in this Tribunal as I.D. No.37/205 and notices were issued to the parties concerned. 
2: The averments made is the claim statement are as follows:- 


It is submitted that Petitioner was appointed as Badli Filler on 6.9.2006 in the Respondent company. It is 
submitted that from the date of appointment, Petitioner was regular to his duties and performing duties upto the 
satisfaction of one and all. While the matters stood thus, charge sheet dt.9.2.2008 was issued alleging that he 
remained absent during the year 2007, as such, it amounts to misconduct under company's standing order 
No.25.25. Petitioner submitted his explanation dt.4.3.2008. However, without considering any of the submissions 
made by him, an enquiry was conducted with a predetermined notion, as if Petitioner absented for duties willfully. 
During the enquiry it was categorically pleaded that, as Petitioner was suffering with ill-health and also as his 
uncle (Father s brother) passed away, hence he could not be regular to duties. In fact, he was not given any 
opportunity much less valid in nature. Basing on such lop sided enquiry, enquiry officer held the charges as 
proved. Thereafter, a show cause notice dt.29/3 -03-2008, was issued to Petitioner and Petitioner submitted his 
reply. But, without considering any of the submissions made, basing on the erroneous findings of the enquiry 
officer, Petitioner was dismissed from service with effect from 9.5.2008 vide office order dt. 7/9.5.2008. It is 
submitted that during the course of enquiry, Petitioner categorically pleaded his inability to be regular to duty, was 
only on account of the ill health as well as uncle of the Petitioner passed away during that time. Further, he also 
pleaded that, he will attend for duty without absence in future. Unfortunately, without considering any of the above 
submissions, Petitioner was dismissed from service w.e.f. 9.5.2008 vide office order dt.l7/9.5.2008. It is 
submitted that the action of the Respondent in dismissing from service is wholly illegal, arbitrary violative of 
principles of natural justice. Enquiry Officer grossly erred in holding the charges as proved. The whole enquiry 
was conducted in a routine and mechanical manner with a predetermined intention to somehow or the other, put 
me to extreme hardship of dismissal from service. Before issuing the impugned order of dismissal, approval of 
competent authority was not obtained, as per the standing orders. No opportunity was given to the Petitioner to 
produce witnesses on his behalf. Had any opportunity was given to him to produce witnesses on my behalf, after 
explaining the procedure of enquiry, Petitioner could have produced witnesses on my behalf, thereby the necessity 
to issue the impugned order of dismissal could have been avoided. Neither the findings of the Enquiry Officer, 
nor the impugned order does not give any reasons, much less ‘valid in nature. The enquiry officer relied upon the 
evidence of irrelevant witnesses, who have no personal knowledge of the charge alleged against the Petitioner. 
Though, enquiry officer relied upon several documents to substantiate the charges, none of those documents either 
shown or furnished to him either before or during the course of enquiry. Even otherwise also, even the marked 
documents do not establish the charge alleged against him. The Respondent failed to apply his mind 
independently while issuing the impugned office order of dismissal त. 7/9-05-2008, as he did not delve into the 
alleged misconduct and the punishment proposed to be inflicted on the Petitioner. Before commencement of 
enquiry, the procedure of enquiry was not explained and Petitioner was not offered the assistance of any defense 
assistance. Neither the proceedings of enquiry were conducted in the language known to the Petitioner nor was 
explained in the language known to him. In fact, as per the instructions issued by the Respondent company, the 
proceedings of enquiry are to be conducted in the language known to the delinquent employee. The findings of the 
enquiry officer are not only contrary to the evidence on record, but also self-contradictory. The findings of the 
Disciplinary Authority are outside the scope of charge sheet. It is further submitted that Petitioner is the sole 
breadwinner of his family. As a result of dismissal, his whole family rendered without any livelihood. It is 
submitted that for the reasons mentioned above, the punishment of dismissal from service is too harsh, excessive 
and disproportionate to the charges alleged. Before imposing a major penalty of dismissal from service, the 
Disciplinary Authority ought to have considered the issue of imposing any minor penalty. It is prayed for 
indulgence of this Hon'ble Court to modify the punishment of dismissal, to that of any other lesser penalty. It is 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5679 


submitted that a conciliation was moved before the conciliation officer which ended in failure. It is therefore 
prayed that to set aside the dismissal order and direct the Respondent for reinstatement of the Petitioner with all 
consequential benefits. 


3. Respondent filed counter denying the averments of the Petitioner_as under: 


It is submitted that Petitioner was dismissed from the services of the Respondent Company on proved charge of 
absenteeism vide Letter No.BPA/PER/29/739, dated 9.5.2008 with immediate effect. It is apparently clear 
that there is an abnormal delay of about 6 years in raising the dispute by the Petitioner and therefore the Petition is 
liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and latches. It is prayed that this Hon'ble Tribunal may decide the 
delay in raising the dispute as a preliminary issue. It is submitted that the delinquent workman was dismissed on 
proved charges after conducting a detailed domestic enquiry duly following the Principles of Natural Justice. It is 
submitted that the Petitioner was initially appointed 6.09.2006 as a Badli Filler at Goleti-l incline Bellampalli 
Area. While he was working in Goleti-! Incline, Bellampalli Area, he had put in just 68 musters during the 
calendar year 2007 and remained absent to duties unauthorisedly on all other days in the year, which constituted 
misconduct under Company's Standing Orders No.25.25 and 25.3] for the misconduct committed by him. It is 
submitted that the Petitioner was issued a Charge Sheet No.BPAGLT.I/R8/6l6 DATED 09.02.2008 under 
Company's Standing Orders 25.25 and 25.3] for his habitual absenteeism and absence from duty without 
sanctioned leave or sufficient cause during the year 2007. In receipt of Charge sheet, Petitioner submitted the 
explanation to the charge sheet. It is submitted that Petitioner was served with a letter advising him to appear for 
enquiry at Goleti-l incline Bellampalli Area on 05.03.2008 with all documents and witnesses. Accordingly, 
Petitioner appeared before enquiry officer and participated in the enquiry proceedings without any pretext what so 
ever in nature and he was given full and fair opportunity to defend his case. It is submitted that on the basis of 
evidence on record the enquiry officer submitted his report holding that the charges levelled against Petitioner 
were proved under Company's Standing orders No.25.25. and 25.3l. It is submitted that the Disciplinary 
Authority after going through the entire Enquiry Proceedings, and after evaluating all the evidence on record, 
concurred with the finding of the Enquiry Officer. Since the charges levelled and proved in the enquiry were of 
grave and serious in nature warranting punishment of dismissal and after considering his attendance over the years 
viz. 2006-2008 musters, and after finding that there was no improvement in his attendance, and as there was no 
extenuating circumstances to take a lenient view, the Petitioner was dismissed from the services of the company 
vide letter No.BPA/PER/29/739, dated 7/l9.5.2008 with immediate effect. It is submitted that the Petitioner 
was a chronic and habitual absentee and did not put in at least !90 attendances as expected from an underground 
workman during the years 2006 and 2008. Further, he remained absent from duty without sanctioned leave, sick 
or sufficient cause and did not bother to communicate to the unit authorities about his inability to attend to duties. 
The Petitioner did not, at least inform or communicate the reasons of his absence to the mine authorities at any 
point of time, which clearly establish the fact that he was not interested in his job. The contention of the Petitioner 
that due to his uncle’s death in accident he could not attend the duties, but Petitioner could not produce any 
certificate or medical records neither before enquiry officer nor before this Hon'ble Tribunal to substantiate his 
absenteeism. Therefore, the contentions of the Petitioner are denied, and it is only an after thought to make out a 
defense in his favour, and the Petitioner is to put to strict proof of the same. It is submitted that the Petitioner 
raised the dispute in the year 20I3, ie. after a lapse of 6 years from the date of dismissal, which shows his 
disinterest towards his duties. It is submitted that the Petitioner should have been more careful and conscious of 
his responsibilities, towards his family members and towards his job. He failed to realize his mistake inspite of 
giving opportunities and paid no heed to the advice of his higher authorities in regard to be regular to duties. For 
the fault and mistakes of the Petitioner he cannot hold the Respondent Company responsible. It is the Petitioner 
himself who has to be blamed for this situation, which is the result of his negligent behavior and callous attitude 
towards his job. As such the allegations of the Petitioner are wholly untenable and devoid of any merits, hence 
denied. The Respondent Company at present employees about 44,000 persons, which includes workmen, 
executives and supervisors. The production results will depend upon the overall attendance and performance of 
each and every individual. They are inter-linked and inseparable. In this regard, if any one remains absent, 
without prior leave or without any justified cause, the work to be performed get affected. Such unauthorised 
absence creates sudden void, which at time is very difficult to fill-up, and there will be no proper planning and 
already planned schedules get suddenly disturbed without prior notice. That is the reason why the Respondent's 
Company is compelled to take severe action against the unauthorized absentee having put in less musters. The 
Petitioner had put in 34 musters during the year 2006, 68 musters during the year 2007 and 5 musters up to 
March,2008. As such the Respondent Company was constrained to dismiss the Petitioner for unauthorized 
absenteeism with effect from 9.05.2008. In view of above, it is prayed to dismiss the claim petition as devoid of 
merits. 


4. On the basis of rival contentions and pleadings of both the parties, following issues emerge for 
determination:- 
I Whether the departmental enquiry held against the workmen is the legal and valid? 


Il. Whether the industrial dispute raised by development is barred by delay and latches?

गा. Whether the action of the Respondent management in terminating the services of the workmen Sri Jella 
Balaiah vide order dated 9.5.2008 is legal and justified? 


Il. To what relief if any the Petitioner is entitled? 
Findings:- 


5. Issue _No.I: - the departmental enquiry held against the Workman has been held legal and valid word 
order dated 22.7.2023 as the Workman has conceded the validity and legality of the departmental enquiry. 


Therefore, the issue decided accordingly. 


6. Issue No.II:- Undisputedly in the present matter Petitioner has been terminated from service vide order 
dated 9'" May 2008 and present industrial dispute has been raised by the Petitioner in the year 205 after seven 
years from the date of his termination, Petitioner has not furnished any explanation in his petition for such 
inordinate delay in raising the industrial dispute against termination order. 


In this context, reference of few decisions of Hon’ble Supreme Court are relevant as discussed hereunder:- 
In K R Reddy Vs. Industrial Tribunal-II, Hyderabad, Hon’ble Court held:- 


“The Supreme Court extensively considered the scope of relevant provisions and precedent decisions and held 
that there was inordinate, unexplained delay in referring the dispute.” 


In the case of Assistant Engineer, CAD, Kota and Dhan Kumwar, CA No.6473, 2006 III LLJ, the Hon'ble 
Apex Court have held: 


“workman raising the dispute eight years after termination of service —therefore relief by Labour Court should 
not have been granted to workman.” 


In Haryana State Co-operative Land Development Bank and Neelam, 2005 I LLJ, the Apex Court held: 


“Though no time limit prescribed for raising industrial dispute, but stale claim, could not be entertained - 
approaching Labour Court after delay of more than 7 years. Held:- justified refusal of relief in this case.” 


In the case of Sri Prabhakar Vs. Joint Director Sericulture Department in Civil Appeal decision dated 
7.9.I5 Hon'ble Apex Court have held:- 


“40) On the basis of aforesaid discussion, we summarise the legal position as under: 


“An industrial dispute has to be referred by the appropriate Government for adjudication and the workman 
cannot approach the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal directly, except in those cases which are covered 
by Section 2A of the Act. Reference is made under Section 70 of the Act in those cases where the appropriate 
Government forms an opinion that ‘any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended’. The words ‘industrial 
dispute exists’ are of paramount importance unless there is an existence of an industrial dispute (or the 
dispute is apprehended or it is apprehended such a dispute may arise in near future), no reference is to be 
made. Thus, existence or apprehension of an industrial dispute is a sine qua non for making the reference. 
No doubt, at the time of taking a decision whether a reference is to be made or not, the appropriate 
Government is not to go into the merits of the dispute. Making of reference is only an administrative 
function. At the same time, on the basis of material on record, satisfaction of the existence of the industrial 
dispute or the apprehension of an industrial dispute is necessary. Such existence/apprehension of industrial 
dispute, thus, becomes a condition precedent, though it will be only subjective satisfaction based on material 
on record. Since, we are not concerned with the satisfaction dealing with cases where there is apprehended 
industrial dispute, discussion that follows would confine to existence of an industrial dispute. Dispute or 
difference arises when one party make a demand and other party rejects the same. It is held by this Court in 
number of cases that before raising the industrial dispute making of demand is a necessary pre-condition. In 
such a scenario, if the services of a workman are terminated and he does not make the demand and/or raise 
the issue alleging wrongful termination immediately thereafter or within reasonable time and raises the 
same after considerable lapse of period, whether it can be said that industrial dispute still exist. Since there 
is no period of limitation, it gives right to the workman to raise the dispute even belatedly. However, if the 
dispute is raised after a long period, it has to be seen as to whether such a dispute still exists? Thus, 
notwithstanding the fact that law of limitation does not apply, it is to be shown by the workman that there is 
a dispute in praesenti. For this purpose, he has to demonstrate that even if considerable period has lapsed 
and there are laches and delays, such delay has not resulted into making the industrial dispute seized to 
exist. Therefore, if the workman is able to give satisfactory explanation for these laches and delays and 
demonstrate that the circumstances discloses that issue is still alive, delay would not come in his way 
because of the reason that law of limitation has no application. On the other hand, if because of such delay 
dispute no longer remains alive and is to be treated as “dead”, then it would be non-existent dispute which 
cannot be referred. Take, for example, a case where the workman issues notice after his termination, 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 568 


questioning the termination and demanding reinstatement. He is able to show that there were discussions 
from time to time and the parties were trying to sort out the matter amicably. Or he is able to show that there 
were assurances by the Management to the effect that he would be taken back in service and because of these 
reasons, he did not immediately raise the dispute by approaching the labour authorities seeking reference or 
did not invoke the remedy under Section 2A of the Act. In such a scenario, it can be treated that the dispute 
was live and existing as the workman never abandoned his right. However, in this very example, even if the 
notice of demand was sent but it did not evoke any positive response or there was specific rejection by the 
Management of his demand contained in the notice and thereafter he sleeps over the matter for number of 
years, it can be treated that he accepted the factum of his termination and rejection thereof by the 
Management and acquiesced into the said rejection. Take another example. A workman approaches the Civil 
Court by filing a suit against his termination which was pending for number of years and was ultimately 
dismissed on the ground that Civil Court did not have jurisdiction to enforce the contract of personal service 
and does not grant any reinstatement. At that stage, when the suit is dismissed or he withdraws that suit and 
then involves the machinery under the Act, it can lead to the conclusion that dispute is still alive as the 
workman had not accepted the termination but was agitating the same; albeit in a wrong forum. In contrast, 
in those cases where there was no agitation by the workman against his termination and the dispute is raised 
belatedly and the delay or laches remain unexplained, it would be presumed that he had waived his right or 
acquiesced into the act of termination and, therefore, at the time when the dispute is raised it had become 
stale and was not an ‘existing dispute’. In such circumstances, the appropriate Government can refuse to 
make reference. In the alternative, the Labour Court/Industrial Court can also hold that there is no 
“industrial dispute” within the meaning of Section 2(k) of the Act and, therefore, no relief can be granted. 


447) We may hasten to clarify that in those cases where the Court finds that dispute still existed, though raised 
belatedly, it is always permissible for the Court to take the aspect of delay into consideration and mould the relief. 
In such cases, it is still open for the Court to either grant reinstatement without back wages or lesser back wages 
or grant compensation instead of reinstatement. We are of the opinion that the law on this issue has to be applied 
in the aforesaid perspective in such matters.” 


Moreover, in the case of Chief Engineer (Construction) Vs. Keshav Rao, 2005 JCR 96, Hon’ble Supreme 
Court have held that, the delay of a one year and five months in issuing a notice appears to us to be significant. 
Here, in the present matter workman has not issued any notice or raised dispute against his termination in any 
forum for a long period of about fourteen years and his claim against dismissal has become stale due to inordinate 
delay and latches. 


Vs Therefore, in view of the fore gone discussion and law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the 
instant case industrial dispute has been raised by Workman in the year 20I5 against his termination order dated 
7/i9.5.2008 after a lapse of 7 years and has not furnished any explanation for such inordinate delay. Thus, the 
present dispute of Petitioner against termination order has become stale and not maintainable. Therefore, the 
petition filed by the Workman is not maintainable due to inordinate delay and latches and such a dispute has 
become stale and hence not maintainable. 


This issue is decided against the Workman and in favour of the Respondent. 


8. Issue _No.III:- Respondent submitted that Petitioner was appointed as badli filler on l6.9.2006 at 
Goleti-! inc., Bellampalli area and while he was working there so he has put in just 68 musters during the calendar 
year 2007 and remained absent from duties unauthorisedly on all other days in the year which constituted 
misconduct under the Company’s Standing Order No.25.25 and 25.3l. Further, Respondent submitted that the 
Petitioner was issued with chargesheet dated 9.2.2008 was issued to him under Company’s Standing Order 
No.25.25 and 25.3] for his habitual absenteeism and absence from duty without sanctioned leave or sufficient 
cause during the year 2007. After receipt of the chargesheet the Petitioner had submitted his explanation to the 
charge sheet, and Petitioner appeared before the enquiry and participated in the enquiry proceedings without any 
pretext whatsoever in nature and he was given full and fair opportunity to defend his case. Further, Respondent 
contended that basing on the evidence on record, Enquiry Officer submitted his report holding that the charges 
levelled against the Petitioner were proved under Company’s Standing Orders as mentioned in the chargesheet. 
Further, it is submitted that Disciplinary Authority after going through the entire enquiry proceedings and after 
evaluating all the evidence on record conferred with the finding of the Enquiry Officer. Since the charges levelled 
and proved in the enquiry were of grave and serious in nature warranting punishment of dismissal and after 
considering his attendance over the years i.e., 2006-2008 musters, and after finding that there was no improvement 
in his attendance, and as there was no extenuating circumstances to take a lenient view. The Disciplinary 
Authority dismissed the Petitioner from services of the company vide order dated !9.5.2008 with immediate 
effect. Further, it is submitted that Petitioner was a chronic and habitual absentee and did not put in at least 90 
attendances as expected from an underground Workman during the years 2006 and 2008. Further, Petitioner 
remained absent without sanctioned leave, sick or sufficient cause and did not bother to communicate to the unit 
authorities about his inability to attend to duties. Further, it is submitted that Petitioner has submitted that due his 
uncle’s death in accident he could not attend the duties but Petitioner could not produce any certificate or medical 


5682 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


records neither before Enquiry Officer to substantiate his plea of absenteeism. Further, Respondent submitted that 
the pleas of Petitioner are denied and it is only an afterthought to make out a defence in his favour and the 
Petitioner is put to strict proof of the same. 


9. In view of the submissions made by either parties perused the record of enquiry proceedings. Record of 
enquiry proceeding goes to reveal that Petitioner was served with chargesheet dated 9.2.2008 and wherein it is 
alleged against CSE workman that he has put in only 68 days musters for !90 musters in a calendar year 2007. 
Further, said record goes to show that the management has examined two witnesses during the enquiry proceeding 
in support of the charge and management witnesses has given the evidence that the Workman remained habitually 
absent from duty unauthorisedly without sanction of leave and he has put in only 68 musters in the year 2007. 
Although, the CSE Workman was accorded cross examination from these witnesses opportunity but he did not 
avail of it. The statement of the CSE Workman was recorded during Enquiry and in his statement Workman has 
admitted that he was absent from duty on the number of days mentioned in the charge sheet during the year 2007 
but he was absent from duty due to ill-health and elder father (uncle) expired. Further, workman stated that he did 
not report at company’s hospital for treatment or for sick, unfit and he do not have any record to defend his case. 
Further, in cross examination CSE Workman states that he did not apply for leave, sick or send information about 
his absence from duty to the management and did not report sick at company’s hospital for treatment for sick, 
unfit. Further, Workman admitted that he has no record and he remained absent from duty on the dates as 
mentioned in the charge sheet on his own. 


0. Thus, in view of the aforesaid statement of the CSE Workman and evidence recorded during the enquiry 
proceeding, the charge against the CSE Workman was found established under Standing Order No.25.25 for 
habitual absenteeism from the duty. Further, record reveals that show cause notice was served upon the CSE 
Workman for submitting his representation against the finding contained in the enquiry report and that got received 
by the Workman as _ per acknowledgement. Thereafter Disciplinary Authority after considering all the evidence 
and extenuating factors, passed the dismissal order dated 9.5.2008, finding the charge against workman grave and 
serious. Therefore, there is no illegality or impropriety or infirmity in the dismissal order of the Petitioner, passed 
by Respondent management. 


ll. Although Workman has taken plea that he remained absent during the year 2007 due to the reason that he 
was suffering from ill-health and also his uncle passed away and he could not be regular on duty. But Petitioner 
failed to produce any documents to substantiate his plea of illness. Therefore, for the want of any documentary 
evidence i.e., prescriptions of medical practitioner about his treatment of illness or medical certificate of unfit from 
competent medical practitioner. This plea of workman is not tenable. Further, workman failed to explain that 
why he could not report to the Company’s hospital about his sickness or report about his absenteeism to the 
Respondent. Therefore, for the want of above stated documentary evidence, the plea of illness taken by the 
Workman is nothing but ruse and feeble ground and same is not tenable. 


In this context, Hon’ble Supreme Court in Delhi Transport Corporation vs Sardar Singh 2004 SC 574 have 
held, that an employee absents himself from the duty even without sanctioned leave for a very long period, prima 
facie shows lack of interest in the work and the authority can on the basis of record come to the conclusion about 
employee being habitual negligent in duties and exhibited the lack of interest in the employers work, the burden is 
on employee who claimed that there is no negligence and lack of interest to establish it by placing the relevant 
material. But in the present case Petitioner utterly failed to produce any material in evidence to substantiate his 
plea of illness hence, he has rightly been held guilty of committing misconduct under Company’s Standing Order 
No.25.25 for habitual absenteeism from duty. 


Further, Hon’ble Supreme Court in its number of decisions have held that workman remaining absent from duty 
for a long time is a grave misconduct , few decisions of Hon’ble Courts are discussed hereunder: - 


In State of U.P. V. Ashok Kumar Singh 996 () SCC 302, wherein the Apex Court had held: - 


“Having notices the fact that the first Respondent has absented himself from duty without level on several 
occasions, we are unable to appreciate the High Court's observation that ‘his absence from duty would not amount 
to such a grave charge. Even otherwise on the facts of this case, there was no justification for the High Court to 
interfere with the punishment holding that 'the punishment does not commensurate with the gravity of the charge’ 
especially when the High Court concurred with the findings of the Tribunal on facts. No case for interference with 
the punishment is made out.” 


In the case of North Eastern Karnataka R.T. Corpn. v. Ashappa decided on 2 May, 2006 wherein, the Apex 
Court had held:- 


“Remaining absent for a long time, in our opinion, cannot be said to be a minor misconduct. The Appellant runs a 
fleet of buses. It is a statutory organization. It has to provide public utility services. For running the buses, the 
service of the conductor is imperative. No employer running a fleet of buses can allow an employee to remain 
absent for a long time. The Respondent had been given opportunities to resume his duties. Despite such notices, 
he remained absent. He was found not only to have remained absent for a period of more than three years, his 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5683 


leave records were seen and it was found that he remained unauthorisedly absent on several occasions. In this 
view of the matter, it cannot be said that the misconduct committed by the Respondent herein has to be treated 
lightly. 

In Delhi Transport Corporation v. Sardar Singh [(2004) 7 SCC 574], the Apex Court held-: 


"II. Conclusions regarding negligence and lack of interest can be arrived at by looking into the period of 
absence, more particularly, when same is unauthorised. Burden is on the employee who claims that there was no 
negligence and/or lack of interest to establish it by placing relevant materials. Clause (ii) of para 4 of the Standing 
Orders shows the seriousness attached to habitual absence. In clause (i) thereof, there is requirement of prior 
permission. Only exception made is in case of sudden illness. There also conditions are stipulated, non-observance 
of which renders the absence unauthorised." 

State of U.P. v. Sheo Shanker Lal Srivastava and Others [(2006) 3 SCC 276], 
it was opined that, “the Industrial Courts or the High Courts would not normally interfere with the quantum 
of punishment imposed upon by the Respondent stating: "It is now well-settled that principles of law that the 
High Court or the Tribunal in exercise of its power of judicial review would not normally interfere with the 
quantum of punishment. Doctrine of proportionality can be invoked only under certain situations. It is now 
well-settled that the High Court shall be very slow in interfering with the quantum of punishment unless it is 
found to be shocking to one's conscience." 
The Hon’ble Apex Court in the case of Management Coal India Ltd. v. Mukul Kumar Choudhary Civil 
Appeal 5762-5763 of 2009 decided on 24.08.2009 laid down the test of proportionality of punishment and 
held:- 
“One of the test to be applied while dealing with the question of punishment would be: would any 
reasonable employer have imposed such punishment in like circumstances? Obviously, a reasonable 
employer is expected to take into consideration measure, magnitude and degree of misconduct and all other 
relevant circumstances and exclude irrelevant matters before imposing punishment.” 

In the case of Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation Vs. Dilip Uttam Jayabhay, the 2022 LLR 
page 26, wherein the Hon’ble Apex Court held:- 

“once the enquiry finding is held to be fair and proper, industrial Tribunal or Labour Court lacks jurisdiction to 
interfere with the quantum of punishment unless the same is shockingly disproportionate to the gravity of 
conduct.” 

Thus, in view of the fore gone discussion, I am of the considered view that the termination order of the Workman 
from service passed by the Respondent management is legal and justified and said dismissal order of Petitioner is 
liable to be confirmed. 

This issue is decided against the workman and in favour of the Respondent. 


2. Issue No.IV:- In view of the finding given in Issues No. I, I, HI & IV, the Petitioner is not entitled to 
get any relief and present petition is found to be devoid of merit, hence, liable to be dismissed. 


Therefore, Issue No.III is decided accordingly. 
AWARD 


In view of the fore gone discussion and law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court as discussed above, the 
action of the General Manager, M/s. Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., Bellampalli Area, Goleti Township 
(P.O.), Adilabad Distt., in terminating the services of Sri Jellala Balaiah, Ex-Badli Filler, Goleti-! Inc, SCCo. Ltd., 
Bellampalli Area with effect from 9.5.2008 is held legal and justified. The workman is not entitled to any relief 
as prayed for. Reference is answered accordingly. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

This case coming before me for final hearing in the presence of Sri Gulla Ramesh, Advocate for the 
Petitioner/Workman and of Sri T. Ravinder Singh, Advocate for the Respondents/Management and having been 
heard and having stood over for consideration till this day, the Tribunal delivered the following:- 

AWARD:- 


This petition is filed U/Sec.2-A (2) of ILD. Act praying to set aside the dismissal order dt.25.0!.202] 
passed by the Respondent No.2 and direct the Respondents’ Corporation to reinstate the petitioner into service with 
continuity of service, together with all attendant benefits and full back wages. 


2. The brief averments of the petition are as follows:-

enquiry in the absence of petitioner and dismissed him from 25.0!.202l. He incurred huge expenditure for

his illness which given rise to family disputes and suffered physical trauma and mental agony. 


2(b). The petitioner reported back to his duty after his sickness and he was informed that he was dismissed from

2(c). The petitioner, ever since his unjust dismissal from service, could not secure any other alternative

absentee who did not change his attitude in-spite of several opportunities as such the Respondent Company was 
constrained to dismiss him by following due process of law; as such the I.D is not maintainable.

sick at Respondents’ Company hospitals and failed to improve his attendance even after (06) years of appointment 
and the Respondents/Company was constrained to dismiss him for his misconduct in the year 2020 after following 
the principles of natural justice and due process of Law. 


3(d). The petitioner’s negligent attitude in not improving his attendance in spite of several charge sheets and 
penalty is the cause for his dismissal. The Respondent Company runs chain of Hospitals and renders free medical 
service to its employees and it even refer severe medical issues to Corporate Medical Hospitals at Hyderabad. But, 
he failed to avail the privilege & welfare schemes provided by the Respondent Company and he is responsible for 
incurring huge expenses. In the year of appointment i.e., 20l4 he has put in (!0l) musters which is less than

attitude and continued to be absent from duty. Accordingly, in the year 20l8 he was once again Charge sheeted for 
the absenteeism in the year 20l7. However giving another opportunity to improve himself, a lenient view was 
taken by the Management/Respondents and he was imposed penalty for stoppage of (ONE) increment without 
cumulative effect vide letter. Further he failed to change his attitude even after imposition of penalty and still 
remained absence, as such he was once again charge sheeted for the absenteeism in the year 208. However giving 
another opportunity to improve himself a lenient view has been taken and he was imposed penalty for stoppage of 
(ONE) increment without cumulative effect. 


3(e). Further, the production results will depend upon the overall attendance and performance of each every

performed gets effected. Such unauthorized absence creates sudden void, which at times is very difficult to fill-up 
with substitute, and there will be no proper planning and already planned schedules get suddenly disturbed without 
prior notice. For that reason un-authorized absence is viewed seriously, because it will not only affect the 
production and also create burden on the remaining workers. The petitioner during the period from January, 209

No.25.25 and 25.3l, he was charge sheeted vide charge sheet dt.l9.03.2020, directing him to submit his

Management witness has submitted unbiased finding holding the charges proved vide enquiry proceedings and 
Report dt.2.07.2020. As the charges leveled against the petitioner were proved, the copy of enquiry report was

sent to his residential address vide letter dt.2.0.2020 to submit his written representation within (07) days of the

है Whether this Industrial Dispute is maintainable before this Tribunal or not?

7. From the pleadings of Petitioner/Workman and Respondents’/ Company, these are the admitted facts that the 
Petitioner/ Workman was working as Badli Filler in Respondents’/ Company and he was dismissed from service

I is dismissal order dt.25.0.202l. Ex.W-2 is Increment stopped punishment order .30.[.2020 and Ex.W-3 is 
seven days notice on exparte enquiry report dt.07.l0.2020. The above documents of both sides are not in much 
dispute by either side. 


8. Here, on the point of jurisdiction, the learned counsel for the Petitioner has put forth and set forth that as per the 
Division Bench Judgment of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 997 (III) LLJ (Supp.) ll, Between: U. 
Chinnappa Vs. Cotton Corporation of India, this Tribunal has jurisdiction over Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., 
to entertain the Industrial Dispute raised by the petitioner though the appropriate Government is Central 
Government. The petitioner need not raise the Industrial Dispute compulsorily before the Central Government 
Industrial Tribunal, Hyderabad alone, as contended by the respondents’ company. Hence, this I.D petition filed by 
the petitioner is well maintainable before this Tribunal for adjudication of the dispute on merits. 


8(a). The learned counsel for the Petitioner further put forth and set forth that the Petitioner was re-appointed as 
Badli Worker during the year 204. He fell sick and bed-ridden in his native place due to Astama, Skin allergy, 
ENT and joints problems. He was not in a possession to move from the bed and he was constrained to take 
treatment at various hospitals. He lodged an application to the respondents’ company to refer him to company 
attached hospitals for better treatment. The company referred the petitioner for treatment from the corporate 
hospitals but he was not recovered. But, without considering his illness, the period was treated as absent, 
conducted exparte enquiry in the absence of petitioner and dismissed him from 25.0!.202l. He incurred huge 
expenditure for aliments and was compiled to make debts with friends and relatives. Further, the capital 
punishment of dismissal from service is extremely harsh and shockingly disproportionate to the gravity of the 
charges. It was a direct blow on his stomach and the management with one stroke of dismissal, shattered his life at 
into pieces. Therefore, he prays to set aside the dismissal order and direct the respondent’s company to reinstate 
the petitioner into service with continuity of service, together with all attendant benefits and full back wages. 


9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents’/company strenuously put forth and set forth that the 
petitioner was initially appointed as badli-filler on !2.07.2007. He was a chronic absentee and he did not put-in the 
required musters in any calendar year through-out his service. He did not change his attitude and failed to attend 


5688 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


duties regularly. In the due course as the petitioner failed to put-in required musters, he was again issued charge 
sheet for habitual absenteeism without any sufficient cause and without any sanctioned leave which is misconduct 
under clause 25.25 & 25.3] of the Respondent Company Standing orders. The relevant clause of standing orders 
reads as under: 


“Clause 25.25 — Habitual late attendance or habitual absence from duty without sufficient cause.” 


”Clause 25. 34 — Absence from duty without sanctioned leave or sufficient cause or overstaying beyond sanctioned 
leave.” 


9(a). The learned counsel for the respondents’/company further put forth and set forth that the petitioner received 
the charge sheet but did not submit any explanation. Though he received the enquiry notice, he did not choose to 
appear the enquiry officer and not availed the opportunity to defend himself. The Enquiry Officer conducted 
enquiry duly following the principles of natural justice. The Enquiry Officer submitted his findings report by 
holding the petitioner guilty of charges and misconduct under standing orders. The petitioner did not submit any 
representation on the enquiry findings report also. The Respondent Company having found no extenuating 
circumstances to take a lenient view, was constrained to impose the punishment of dismissal from service vide 
Proc. dt.25.0!.202] which is legal and valid. Further, his appeal dt.l8.02.202! was rightly dismissed by the 
competent authority by dismissal order, vide Proc. dt.27.08.202l. There is no victimization and punishment of 
dismissal is not harsh and the Respondent Company was very much correct in imposing the punishment of 
dismissal because of the misconduct and the reckless attitude of the Petitioner. Further, the habitual absenteeism 
creates lot of _ indiscipline among the workers, disturb the working system and also causing financial burden due 
to extending the benefits though they are not contributing for the production and productivity. Therefore, he prayed 
to dismiss the petition and not to grant any relief to the petitioner/workman. 


POINT [४०.।: 


0. Here, on the point of territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal, it is settled Law that as per the Division Bench 
Judgment of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 997 (III) LLJ (Supp.) l, Between: U. Chinnappa Vs. Cotton 
Corporation of India, this Tribunal has got every jurisdiction to entertain the Industrial Dispute raised by the 
petitioner/workman who was an employee of Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., Even though, the Central Govt. 
is appropriate Govt., for the respondents’-Company, the petitioner need not compulsorily raise the Industrial 
Dispute before the Central Govt. Industrial Tribunal, Hyderabad, as contended by the respondents’ company; and 
he can file this I.D. case before this Tribunal as well. Hence, the contentions of the respondents’-company on the 
point of jurisdiction of this Tribunal are not sustainable under Law. Accordingly, it is answered in favour of the 
petitioner and against the respondents’ Singareni Collieries Company Limited. 


POINT No.2: 


Il. In this matter, initially the petitioner/workman has denied the validity and legality of the enquiry report. But 
on 6.06.2025 the learned counsel for petitioner filed Memo U/Sec.ll-A of I.D.Act by accepting the procedure of 
domestic enquiry to be fair and valid. Hence, there is no dispute that the Enquiry Officer has followed the 
principles of natural justice. Now the next question is whether the misconduct is proved in the facts of the case and 
the findings are not perverse. So, this Tribunal is to re-appreciate the evidence and come to its own conclusion with 
regard to finding guilty or not based on evidence. Accordingly, the Point No.| is answered. 


POINT No.3 & 4: 


2. In view of the pleadings of the Petitioner/Workman as well as the Respondents/corporation and rival 
arguments of both sides, now this Court will go into the evidence on record. Admittedly, the petitioner was initially 
appointed as Badli Filler under dependant employment scheme vide office order dt.20.09.2000 and was dismissed 
from service vide office order dt.9.0.2007 alleging absenteeism to duties under Ex.M-], prior to this case. He 
was re-appointed as afresh Badli Filler(UG) at Mandamarri Area vide office Order dt.25.08.20I4 under Ex.M-2, 
and was again dismissed from service vide Office Order dt.25.0.202] under Ex.M-], alleging absenteeism to 
duties. 


3. From a perusal of the record, it is evident that the petitioner absented to duties for (222) days and had put-in 
((00) actual musters during the year 206, for which charge sheet !7.02.207 was issued to the petitioner, which is 
marked as Ex.M-3. The petitioner also absented to duties for (292) days and had put-in only (45) actual musters 
during the year 208, for which charge sheet 3.03.209 was issued to the petitioner, which is marked as Ex.M-5. 
Further, the petitioner again absented to duties for (26l) days and had put-in only (53) actual musters during the 
year 209, for which charge sheet 9.03.2020 was issued to the petitioner, which is marked as Ex.M-6. Domestic 
enquiry was conducted regarding the absenteeism of the petitioner during the year 209 for which Ex.M-5 charge 
sheet dt.9.03.2020 was issued to him. It appears that enquiry notice dt.6.07.2020 under Ex.M-6 was issued to the 
petitioner, but he failed attend the enquiry. From the proceedings of enquiry under Ex.M-7, it appears that the 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5689 


enquiry notice was sent to the petitioner by RPAD on 6.07.2020 advising him to attend the enquiry on 
2.07.2020. He received the same, but did not choose to attend the enquiry. He was called loudly (03) times in 
front of the office of SOM and in the premises, but there was no response. Hence, there was no alternative except 
to conduct the enquiry exparte. 


3(a). Further, the enquiry officer examined Sri B.Balakishan Rao, Acting OS & Presenting Officer; Sri P.Samba 
Reddy, Pay Sheet clerk and P.Chinnamma, General Mazdoor, who deposed in support of the charges framed 
against the petitioner. Further from the Enquiry Report under Ex.M-7, it is clearly evident that the charges were 
amply proved against the petitioner. The petitioner/workman acknowledged the same on 4.0.2020 vide Ack., 
under Ex.M-8. The petitioner did not submit any representation on the enquiry report and the respondents/company 
dismissed him from service vide Proc. dt.25.0.202l which is marked as Ex.M-ll. He submitted appeal 
dt.8.02.202! under Ex.M-l0 stating that his absenteeism was due to ill-health only but not intentional and 
requested to reinstate him into service. However, the said appeal was dismissed vide Proc. 6.27.08.202] by the 
competent authority. Thus, it is evident from the enquiry report under Ex.M-3 as well as the material on record, 
that the petitioner had not put in minimum required musters of (90) and he put-in only (53) musters, during the 
year 209. For which, petitioner submitted in his appeal that due to ill-health and family problems, he was unable 
to perform duty regularly during the charge sheet period. However, it is clear that the petitioner has not attended to 
duties regularly and the charges were proved against him. Therefore, it can be said that the respondents/company 
has no axe to grind against the petitioner. Hence, this Tribunal has no hesitation to hold that the charges leveled 
against the petitioner/workman are proved and misconduct of the petitioner/workman is established basing on the 
evidence and findings of enquiry officer are not perverse. Moreover, this is not the case of loaded dice situation 
against the petitioner/workman by the respondents/corporation. 


4. Here, the contention of the Petitioner/Workman is that he was re-appointed in the year 20I4 and he served the 
company for (5) years and he hails from a very poor family, he has got no other livelihood and facing untold 
financial problems and prayed to consider the case U/Sec.l-A of ID. Act. The ill-health suffered by the petitioner 
and facts and circumstances of the present case amount to mitigating circumstances. 


5. Here, this Tribunal relied on a Division Bench Judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court rendered in Civil 
Appeal No.257/l999, dt.08.04.999 between Ajaib Singh vs. Sirhind Co-op. Marketing-cum-Processing Service 
Society Ltd., & another, wherein their lordships held that: - 


“The object of Industrial Disputes Act was to give succor to weaker sections of the society. The emergence of 
State implies an end to exploitation of workman and as a corollary to that collective bargaining came into it ow 
intended to protect workmen against victimization and exploitation by the employer and to ensure termination of 
peaceful manner. 


“The object of the Act, therefore, is to give succor to weaker sections of the society which is a pre-requisit 
ensure industrial peace and pre-empt industrial tension, the Act further aims at enhancing the industrial productior. 
to be life-blood of a developing society. The Act provides a machinery for investigation and settlement of industr 
legal technicalities with a view to avoid delays, by specially authorized Courts which are not supposed to deny the 
procedural wrangles”. 


5(a). Further, in a decision of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 20l2 (l) ALD 220 (DB), wherein their 
lordships observed that: - 


“The Industrial Disputes Act, /947 is a social welfare legislation, which required to be interpreted 
keeping in view the goals set out in the Preamble and Directive principles of State Policy in Part-IV of the 
Constitution. The Labour Court/Industrial Tribunal is conferred with very wide discretion 9/3$९८/।-4 of the 
Act for granting appropriate relief”’. 


6. Here, their Lordships of the Hon’ble Gujarat High Court in a case rendered on 04.05.994, Between: 
Management of Glaxo India Ltd., Vs. State of Assam and 3 others categorically observed that “a Labour Court is 
required to settle a dispute according to the principles of natural justice, equity and good conscience and law 
without attaching undue importance to legal technicalities”. 


7. Here, it is to be noted that the concept of Industrial Dispute is quite broad and with the passage of time its 
horizon is being expanded. Further, the disputes are required to be resolved for the purpose of establishing peaceful 
and cordial atmosphere in an industry. Peace and harmony are the quintessential aspects which are to be kept in 
view while dealing with the “/is” or “controversy” relating to any industry. Apart from the above, whether the 
impugned punishment is so disproportionate as to shock the conscience of the Court, has to be decided on the facts 
of each case, having due regard to the gravity of misconduct & nature of duties discharged by the delinquent 
employee. 


8. Further, the Hon’ble Madras High Court observed in a case rendered in Management of Hyudai Motor India 
Ltd Vs. T.Sudhakar ... on 377 January, 2022: 


5690 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


“When scales of justice stands balanced in a given case, the tilt to be exercised should be in favour of 
the poor workmen rather than the mighty Managements.” 


9. Therefore, in view of the above mitigating circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the 
extreme punishment of dismissal from service imposed by the respondents/company against the 
petitioner/workman is harsh, disproportionate and shocks to conscience of this Tribunal, hence, deserves to be 
modified since the disciplinary authority cannot be permitted to act arbitrarily and work like a Roman Knight and 
it cannot be allowed a fight between David and Goliath as in the present case on hand. Moreover, the facts of this 
case attracts the proverbial saying “Every saint has a past and every sinner has a future”. Moreover, facts of this 
case attracts the proverbial saying “Every saint has a past and every sinner has a future” and Biblical proverbs 
“Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute” and “Speak up and 
judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.” Further, “Heavens would not have fallen if one more 
opportunity is given for the petitioner”. 


20. This Tribunal has perused, analyzed and meditated upon the case at hand, the case laws and principles of law 
referred above. In view of the above facts and circumstances and keeping in view of the principle “temper justice 
with mercy” and to meet the ends of justice, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the punishment of removal from 
service imposed on the petitioner is disproportionate and shocks the conscience of this Tribunal and hence, it 
deserves to be modified appropriately. Taking a holistic view of the matter, this Tribunal is of considered view that 
the extreme punishment of dismissal from service imposed on the petitioner deserves to be modified. However, 
since the charges leveled against the petitioner are proved, the relief is to be molded by this Tribunal appropriately 
and this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled to be reinstated into service as “Afresh 
Badli Filler” only. Consequently, the petitioner is not entitled to any back wages, any continuity of service and 
any attendant benefits, since petitioner might have gainfully employed during pendency of this Industrial Dispute. 
Hence, the punishment of dismissal from service imposed by the Respondents Company is hereby modified 
appropriately. Accordingly, the Point No.2 & 3 are answered. 


2. IN THE RESULT, the petition is partly allowed. The dismissal order dt.25.0!.202] under Ex.M- passed by 
the Respondent No.2 is hereby modified. The respondents’/company is directed to reinstate the petitioner into 
service as “Afresh Badli Filler” only, but without any continuity of service, without any attendant benefits and 
without any back wages. The petitioner is entitled to the salary only from the date of publication this Award. Copy 
of the Award be sent to the appropriate Government for publication. Both parties shall bear their own costs.
