AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section l0 of 
the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
Order No. L-2202/32/20I3-IR(CM-II) dated 03/0/20l3 has been pleased to refer the following dispute 
between the employer, that is the Management of Nimcha Colliery, Satgram Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited 
and their workmen for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5877 


“Whether the action of the management of Nimcha Colliery under Satgram Area of M/s. E.C. Limited to 
dismiss from service to Sri Antarijami Baratia was proper, fair and proportionate judgement only on 
ground of absenteeism which was due to his illness. If not, so what relief management can provide to 
him?” 


| On receiving Order No. L-2202/32/203-IR(CM-ID) dated 03/0/203 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case No. 8 of 203 was registered on 
4/02/204 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to 
appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Mr. H. L. Soni, Assistant General Secretary of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on 
07/0/205 on behalf of Antarjami Baratia, dismissed workman. Management contested the case by filing written 
statement on 5/03/207. Brief fact of the case, as disclosed in the written statement of the union is that Antarjami 
Baratia was posted as Underground Loader at Nimcha Colliery under Satgram Area of ECL and he did not attend 
duty from 3/05/2008 to 05/09/2008 due to his illness and due to torture by money lenders. Workman reported for 
his duty with medical certificate of his illness but he was not allowed to resume duty. A charge sheet No. 
AGENT/NIM/PD/08/65 dated 06/09/2008 was issued to him. A domestic enquiry was initiated. Workman had no 
information about the enquiry and he was unable to attend the same. Charged workman was not informed about 
appointment of the Enquiry Officer, Management Representatives and the date fixed for enquiry. After lapse of 
about three years management again issued another charge sheet bearing No. NIM/AGT/CS/20I/473 dated 
09/5.04.20. It is contended that second charge sheet was illegal, vague, motivated and had no binding effect 
upon the workman after issuance of first charge sheet. Workman participated in the second enquiry and during 
enquiry proceeding he explained reasons of his absence from duty and he also submitted medical certificates. 
Without considering the reply of the workman, Enquiry Officer concluded the enquiry in perfunctory manner and 
the workman was dismissed. Workman raised an Industrial Dispute before the Assistant Labour Commissioner 
(C), Asansol praying for resumption of duty on 22/06/20l. Workman was dismissed from service of the company 
during pendency of Industrial Dispute and a letter of termination was issued to him by the General Manager 
bearing No. SAT/PER/GM/Termination/!/3094 dated 29.09.20/07.0.20i. It is asserted on behalf of the 
workman that past record of the workman is good. His attendance in work during the year 2005 was 246 days, 
during the year 2006 was 206 days and during the year 2007 was 257 days. It is only due to torture by money 
lenders workman was unable to attend the duty. It is inter alia contended that dismissal of the workman from 
service due to his absence from duty is harsh and disproportionate punishment to the nature of offence. It is further 
stated that during pendency of the proceeding Antarijami Barati expired on 08/07/20I4 and his son, Pabitra Baratia 
was substituted in his place. Union prayed for providing direction upon the management to provide benefits to the 
dependent son of the employee. 


3. Management of ECL in written statement disclosed that Antarjami Baratia was found absent from duty 
from 3/05/2008 without any sanctioned leave and charge sheet was issued against him bearing No. 
AGENT/NIM/PD/08/65 dated 06/09/2008. The workman did not participate in the enquiry and continued to 
remain absent. Subsequently a fresh charge sheet was issued bearing No. NIM/AGT/CS/20/473 dated 
09/5.04.20i] under clause 26.29 of certified standing order of the company. A departmental enquiry was held on 
/08/20 and charged employee participated in the enquiry. Enquiry Officer after concluding enquiry submitted 
his report on 27/08/20ll, where he found the workman guilty of the charge. A letter No. SAT/GM/PER/LAB- 
C/20/2858 dated 0/4.09.20l] was issued to the charged workman seeking explanation. Management after 
considering all materials, terminated the workman from service and communicated the same to him through letter 
No. SAT/PER/GM/Termination/I/3094 dated 29.09.20I/07.0.20Il. Koyala Mazdoor Congress by letter No. 
KMC/ID/20/72 dated 2/06/20] raised the Industrial Dispute. Manager further stated that during pendency of 
the Industrial Dispute, Antarjami Baratia died and his legal heirs have no authority to continue the proceeding. 
According to the management full opportunity was given to the workman in the domestic enquiry. Therefore, 
Industrial Dispute raised by the union is liable to be dismissed. 


4. Union examined Pabitra Baratia, dependent son of Late Antarjami Baratia as Workman Witness-I. He 
filed his affidavit-in-chief and was cross-examined for the first time on 07/02/20l8. Witness was re-examined on 
recall on 06/2/2022 and was re-cross-examined by the management. Pabitra Baratia thereafter did not appear to 
put his signature on evidence recorded on recall on 06/ 2/2022. Documents produced by him have been admitted 
in evidence as follows: 


(i) copy of Enquiry Notice dated 5/7.04.2009 is marked as Exhibit ४४-।. 
(ii) copy of second Notice of enquiry dated | /07/2009 is marked as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) copies of document related to his father’s departmental enquiry, mercy petition, charge sheet and medical 
treatment papers are collectively marked as Exhibit W-3. 


5878 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


5. Management examined Sh. Sumit Choudhary as Management Witness-I. He filed his affidavit-in-chief 
wherein it is stated that workman was a habitual absentee and remained absent without information or sufficient 
reasons. On the last occasion workman was absent from duty from 3!/05/2008 to I5/04/20ll. Workman was 
charge sheeted on 5/04/20ll. Agent appointed the Enquiry Officer by his letter No. AGENT/NIM/PD/556 dated 
26/27.07.20l. Notice of enquiry was served upon the workman vide letter No. AGENT/NIM/PD/20] I/ENQ255 
dated 05/08/20l. Workman appeared and participated in the enquiry. Management has filed copy of enquiry 
proceeding in four pages and enquiry report in two pages which have been admitted in evidence. A second show 
cause Notice dated 0/l4.09.20ll was issued by the General Manager addressed to the workman. Workman 
replied to the second show cause Notice and finally the General Manager dismissed the workman from service 
vide his letter dated 29.09.20/07.0.20. According to the management, dismissal of the workman is justified. 
In course of examination, witness produced the following documents:- 


(i) Copy of Charge Sheet dated 09/5.04.20 issued to the workman for his unauthorized absence from duty 
is produced as Exhibit M-| 


(ii) Copy of letter dated 26/27.07.20 for appointment of the Enquiry Officer is produced as Exhibits M-2. 
(iii) Copy of Notice of enquiry dated 05/08/20! fixing /08/20] for enquiry is produced as Exhibit M-3. 
(iv) Copy of Enquiry proceeding in four pages is collectively produced as Exhibit M-4. 

(v) Copy of Enquiry report in two pages is collectively produced as Exhibit M-S. 


(vi) Copy of second show cause Notice dated 0/4.09.20 issued to the charged employee is produced as 
Exhibit M-6. 


(vii) Copy of reply dated 26/09/20li submitted by the workman against the second show cause Notice is 
produced as Exhibit M-7. 


(viii) | Copy of letter of termination dated 29.09.20/07.0.20I] issued by the General Manager, Satgram Area 
is produced as Exhibit M-8. 


(ix) Copy of medical certificate issued by a private practicing doctor submitted by the concerned workman 
during course of enquiry, is produced as Exhibit M-9. 


In cross-examination, management witness stated that charge levelled against the workman was only due to long 
unauthorized absence and no charge of habitual absence was arraigned against him. Witness admitted that on 
earlier occasion a charge sheet was issued for absenting from duty w.e.f. 3/05/2008. The first departmental 
enquiry was initiated against the workman but it was not completed and a second charge sheet was issued on 
5/04/20 covering entire period of unauthorized absence of the workman from 3/05/2008 till 5/04/20I. It 
further transpires that no final order was passed in respect of the earlier enquiry proceeding. Witness denied that it 
was illegal and improper to issue a second charge sheet for the purpose of computing the entire period of 
unauthorized absence. 


6. Heard argument advanced by Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative on behalf of Koyala Mazdoor 
Congress. It is argued that management of ECL committed illegality by issuing two charge sheets against the 
workman. First charge sheet was dated 06/09/2008 and a domestic enquiry was initiated against the workman but 
without concluding the same, a second charge sheet was issued on 5/04/20ll which is illegal. Union 
representative further argued that workman participated in the second enquiry and he had disclosed that he was 
suffering from illness and he could not attend duty due to torture by moneylenders. It is argued that there were 
sufficient reasons for the absence of the workman. Therefore, the order of dismissal passed against him is required 
to be set aside and management shall pay back wages and all consequential reliefs to Pabitra Baratia, the dependent 
son. 


7. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management in reply argued that workman remained absent from 
duty without leave or permission of the competent authority for three years. A charge sheet was issued against the 
workman and enquiry was initiated but the workman did not participate in the enquiry and the enquiry proceeding 
was discontinued. As workman continued to remain absent, management issued a fresh charge sheet against the 
workman disclosing a charge of unauthorized absence from duty from 3!/05/2008 till date of issue of charge sheet 
i.e. [5/04/20II. On the second occasion, charge sheet was served upon the workman. An enquiry proceeding was 
initiated and workman participated in the enquiry. After concluding of the enquiry workman was found guilty of 
charge under clause 26.29 of certified standing order for his absence from duty for more than ten days without 
information. Enquiry proceeding and findings of the Enquiry Officer were supplied to the charged employee. A 
second show cause Notice (Exhibit M-6) was issued to the workman. He submitted reply (Exhibit M-7) against the 
second show cause Notice and finally after considering all materials on record and enquiry proceeding, General 
Manager, Satgram Area dismissed the workman from service by issuing a letter dated 29.09.20/07.0.20I] 
(Exhibit M-8). Learned advocate submitted that order of dismissal issued against the workman is appropriate, 
proper and consistent with the nature of misconduct. 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5879 


8. Having considered the arguments advanced by the union representative and learned advocate for the 
management, it appears to me that union is harping upon facts that initially charge sheet was issued to the 
workman for his unauthorized absence on 06/09/2008 but without completing the enquiry another charge sheet was 
issued to the workman on 5/04/20ll. According to the union, second charge sheet could not have been issued 
during pendency of the first charge sheet. I have considered facts and circumstances and evidence adduced by 
parties. In the written statement, union stated that workman did not receive any Notice of the first charge sheet and 
also, he did not participate in the enquiry proceeding. I find that neither any final decision was taken in respect of 
the first charge sheet nor did the Enquiry Officer submit his report. The concerned workman continued to remain 
absent and it would appear that he had practically fled his place of work by remaining away for more than two 
years and eleven months. In view of long unauthorized absence, management is always in a position to take 
appropriate action. Management accordingly issued a fresh charge sheet disclosing charge of unauthorized absence 
for a longer period from 3!/05/2008. Copy of charge sheet is produced as Exhibit M-l/Exhibit W-3/3. On the 
second occasion workman participated in the enquiry proceeding. Notice of enquiry was issued to him (Exhibit M- 
3). An enquiry proceeding was conducted on /08/20ll. Copy of the Enquiry proceeding produced has been 
admitted in evidence as Exhibit M-4. It disclosed that charge was proved by the two management representatives, 
namely Tathagata Gupta and S. Tapadar and the charged employee was also present during the enquiry. In the 
Enquiry report, the workman was found guilty of charge. Second show cause Notice was issued and in reply to the 
same, workman reiterated that he was absent due to illness and in fear of torture by the moneylenders. 
Management did not consider such plea as sufficient and plausible reasons for the workman to remain absent from 
duty for such a long period and found it fit to dismiss the workman from service. 


9. I find from the record that Enquiry officer held enquiry in a fair manner by providing opportunity to the 
charged employee to cross-examine the management representatives. Principles of Natural Justice were also duly 
followed. It is unusual and unacceptable that a workman would leave his place of work without any information or 
authorization from the employer and disrupt work by long absence. If the presence of the workman is 
unpredictable in his workplace, management cannot place reliance upon such workman for his participation and 
contribution in his work. He also failed to prove his illness. 


0. In view of my above discussion, I find no illegality in the order of dismissal of workman from service. 
Workman who remained absent for such a long period without proper grounds is detrimental to the interest of the 
employer company. Punishment of dismissal of the workman is accordingly found to be proportionate to the nature 
of misconduct of long absence, without justified cause. To my mind, workman was not justified in remaining 
absent from duty without tenable reasons. I find no merit in the Industrial Dispute and hold that legal heirs of the 
dismissal workman are not entitled to any relief except the dues due to past service. Industrial Dispute is according 
dismissed. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. Legal heirs of the dismissed workman are not entitled to any 
relief except the legal dues arising out of service already rendered by Antarjami Baratia. Let an Award be drawn 
up in the light of my above discussion. Let copies of Award be communicated to the Ministry for information 
and Notification.

l. Outline: Instant Industrial Dispute has been registered for adjudication on the basis of a Reference vide 
Notification No. L-400]/2/20I2-IR(DU) dated 25.02.20I3 under clause (d) of Sub-Section (l) sub-section (2A) of 
Section 0 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947) (hereinafter called the Act), of the Ministry of Labour- 
Government of India as follows:- 


“Whether the action of the management i.e. General Manager Telecom, Shimla Circle in not converting 
the services of Sh. Parveen Kumar S/o Sh. Kisan Chand from part time safai karamchari to full time 
casual labour w.e.f. 77.05.2002 is just, fair and legal, if not to what relief the concerned workman is 
entitled and from which date?.” 


2. The case of Workman/ Petitioner- As per claim statement filed on behalf of workman, he was employed 
as a Part Time sweeper on |5.!2.998 in Telecom Sub-Division Dalhousie. It is said that earlier the father of the 
workman was employed in the Department but due to his ill health the workman was appointed in place of his father 
and a written consent was also taken from both of them on 5.!2.998. In the year 200I the process of converting 
part time employees to full time casual labourer on daily wages started, as per letter of Department dated 
25.08.2000. As per the criteria set out in above said letter dated 25.08.2000, the part time worker who worked 
continuously for 240 days in the department preceding/ last 2 months, they were liable to converted into full time 
casual labourers. It is said that workman fulfilled all conditions as per letter dated 25.08.2000 and was requested to 
fill up proforma and to submit it with the relevant documents by the respondent department to make him full time 
worker. It is further said that the favorite junior co-workers who were part time workers are made full time workers 
because of their personal interest vide Memo No.E-7/PT/Safaiwala/PT-i dated 7.05.2002. But the workman 
Parveen Kumar was denied his conversion into full time casual worker. Whenever the workman consulted 
departmental officer they only assured that he could also be converted into full time casual labourer but no action 
was taken. When grievance of workman was not resolved he raised a dispute before Regional Labour Commissioner 
(Central) / Conciliation Officer through a demand note for amicable settlement. The demand raised was not resolved

and a conciliation failure report was sent to the Ministry by the Regional Labour Commissioner and reference by 
Labour Ministry was sent to the Tribunal for adjudication. It is further stated by the workman that he is still working 
as part time worker but w.e.f. August, 20! onward he has not been paid. It is also stated that workman had made 
several request but nothing has been done in this regard and his wages are still not paid. Through the claim statement 
it is prayed that respondent be directed to regularize the services of workman w.e.f. 7.05.2002 or from the date of 
joining of Junior Employees in regular capacity with all consequential reliefs i.e. Seniority, Arrear of Pay and 
allowance service benefits etc, to pay the part time wages lying pending for the period w.e.f. August, 20] till the 
date, to pay cost of litigation and any other relief as this Court may deem fit and proper. 


3. The case of Management-Respondents- The opposite parties BSNL Authorities have contested the claim 
petition of workman and they have filed their written statement/ reply and objection against the claim petition. 
According to case of management the workman was never appointed on regular post. However, it is admitted by the 
opposite parties BSNL Management that workman was engaged as Part Time Safai Karamchari w.e.f. 0.05.999. 
He could not be converted into full time casual worker as he did not fulfill conditions laid down in the Department 
of Telecom, New Delhi Letter No.269-3/99-STN-II dated 25.08.2000 and Chief G.M. Telecom, H.P. Telecom 
Circle, Shimla Letter No. staff/S-035/8] dated 4..2000. According to further case of management the workman 
has submitted demand notice in year 20!2 which is time barred and stale, therefore, his claim is liable to be 
dismissed. According to contesting opposite parties the workman is not entitled to benefits as per instructions 
contained in letters dated 25.08.2000 and dated 4..2000 as he did not fulfill the conditions laid down by the 
Department of Telecom. According to management the cutoff date is 0.08.998 whereas the workman was engaged 
as Part Time Safai Karamchari on 0.05.999. In further written statement/ reply of management the facts and

According to management his father was working as Part Time Employee since year 970 and he abandoned his 
services on 5.2.998. According to case of opposite parties only dependent of regular employee can claim 
appointment on compassionate ground and therefore no claim of workman Parveen Kumar is sustainable in the 
present case. The management has denied document of salary record annexed and submitted by workman alongwith 
his claim petition as not signed by any BSNL official/ authorities. According to management as per decision of 
Supreme Court in Uma Devi case workman is not entitled to any benefits. It is further stated by the management that 
the workman did not fulfill the conditions laid down in Department letters therefore, he was not converted into full 
time casual labourer on daily wages. The management has however, admitted that workman had earlier represented 
at various levels for his conversion from part time casual labour to full time casual labourer and a suitable reply has 
already been communicated to him vide letter dated 23.08.200. It is also admitted by management that workman 
worked till October, 2004 and wages were paid to him. According to case of management thereafter, the workman 
abandoned his job on his own and therefore consideration of representation- Annexure P-9 to P-8 for salary w.e.f. 
August, 20! does not arise. The workman has raised Industrial Dispute after 7 years and therefore same is liable to 
be dismissed on the ground of limitation.

7. Arguments of Parties: According to Ld. Counsel appearing on behalf of workman although the workman

the present Industrial Dispute and therefore Industrial Dispute may be dismissed.

FINDINGS 


9. Having heard both the parties and after perusal of case record it appears that the present Industrial Dispute 
revolves around the denial of the claim of workman Parveen Kumar for conversion into full time casual labourer 
from part time worker on the ground that he was not fulfilling the required criteria and condition laid down by the 
Telecom Department in its policy letters dated 25.08.2000 and I4.!.2000. The reference which has been received 
for adjudication is also pointing the same question as to whether action of management in not converting the 
services of Parveen Kumar from Part Time Safai Karamchari to full time casual labourer is just fair and legal? The 
two important documents first being Letter No.269-3/99-STN-II dated 25.08.2000 issued from Government of 
India, Department of Telecom Services New Delhi and second document being Letter No.Saff/S-035/8l dated 
4..2000 issued from Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited office of CGMT HP Circle, Shimla are available on the case 
record which are marked as Exhibit/ Annexure P-3 and Ex. W-2]. This two letters are admitted by both the parties 
and not in any dispute. According to case of workman he was fulfilling the required criteria/ conditions as per policy 
contained in this letters whereas according to BSNL Management the workman was not fulfilling the conditions 
mentioned in this Policy letter and therefore he was denied to be converted into full time casual labourer . Let us 
examine what is policy as per above referred two important documents containing the policy of telecom department 
(BSNL) converting part time worker into a full-time causal worker. 


0. It appears that Letter No.269-3/99-STN-II dated 25.08.2000 issued from Government of India was a 
policy decision taken after consultation with Telecom Finance and it was decided that as one time relaxation part 
time casual labors with less than 4 hours of duty per day who had worked for 240 days in the preceding 2 months 
may be converted into full time causal labors. Certain conditions were also mentioned in this letter and as per 
condition No. ix), the orders will take effect from the date of issue of this letter which is 25.08.2000. Meaning 
thereby a part time casual labourer with less than 4 hours of duty if had already worked for atleast 240 days in the 
preceding !2 months from 25.08.2000, he was entitled for conversion into full time casual labourer. In the present 
case workman Parveen Kumar is although claiming that he has been engaged since |5.2.998 but as per admission 
of department he was working since 0.05.999. Even date 0.05.999 which is admitted date by BSNL 
Management is taken to be correct one from the date when the workman Parveen Kumar was engaged as part time 
casual labourer, on the cut off date 25.08.2000 he had already completed more than 240 days. Now adverting to 
another letter dated 4.!.2000 which is Ex. W-2], it is clear that this letter has been issued after incorporation of 
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. for the purpose of regularization of the casual labourers. In this letter issued from Bharat 
Sanchar Nigam Ltd. CGMT, HP Circle, Shimla, earlier letter issued from Department of Telecom Service dated 
25.08.2000 is also referred. Vide this letter dated 4.!.2000 application from all part time causal labourers were 
called for who were working as on 0.08.998 and 25.08.2000. In the said letter even vacant posts in Group D 
(including RM) were also indicated. As per said indication DMA TD was having 63 such vacant posts. The 
prescribed application format attached with abovesaid letter dated 4.l!.2000 mentions at point No.8- whether 
working as part time labourer i) as on 0.08.998 ii) as on 25.08.2000. At Point No.9- No. of days worked from 
26.08.999 to 25.09.2000 is to be mentioned. The application of workman which has been forwarded by SDO (T) 
Dalhousie for the purpose of conversion from Part Time Casual labour into full time casual labour is also available 
on the record and same is marked as Ex. P-5. In this application at Point No.8 & 9, it is specifically mentioned that 
the workman was working from 0.05.999 and had completed 305 days from 26.08.999 to 25.08.2000. It may be 
noticed that in the letter !4.!.2000 issued from Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. Himachal Pradesh Circle, Shimla itself 
two dates are mentioned i.e. 0.08.998 and 25.08.2000 when a part time casual labourer was required to be 
working on these dates. In the case of workman Parveen Kumar first date i.e. 0.08.998 mentioned in the policy 
letter is not applicable as a date on which he was working but second dated 25.08.2000 is applicable as the workman 
is said to be working from 0.05.999 as per BSNL Management itself. In above view of the matter the submission 
of BSNL Management that workman was not fulfilling the required criteria and condition contained in two policy 
letters dated 25.08.2000 and 4..2000 cannot be accepted. It appears that when workman Parveen Kumar was 
denied his right to be converted into full time casual labourer he represented several times with a prayer for 
considering his case also but ultimately his claim of conversion into full time casual labourer was refused and the 
management intimated to him in writing vide letter dated 23.08.20l0 issued from the office of General Manager, 
Telecom District Dharamshala. In the said communication of refusal it has been specifically stated that when 
process for conversion from part time casual labourer into full time casual labourer started in year 2000 as per letter 
dated 4..2000 issued from office of HP Circle, Shimla workman Parveen Kumar was not fulfilling the conditions 
mentioned therein. The reason for refusal as stated in letter dated 23.08.200 is apparently Arbitrary and is against 
the policy itself. Another document dated 24..2009 which is communication between sub-divisional official (T) 
Dalhousie and the DET Admn. GMTD, Dharamshala has been brought on record as Exhibit. Annexure P-8 wherein 
it has been specifically mentioned that as per available record Parveen Kumar had worked 305 days in the year 
999-2000 as part time sweeper @Rs.6.50/- per hour for three hours in a day. It is also mentioned that he worked till 
October, 2004 and after verbal direction of your office (Office of GMTD, Dharamshala) he was removed from Part 
Time Sweeper. This letter itself is a glaring example as to how workman Parveen Kumar has been harassed and 
even removed on a verbal direction when he had already fulfilled condition and criteria for his conversion into full 
time casual labourer . Exhibit/ Annexure P-6 is letter issued from the office of General Manager, Telecom District, 


5884 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Dharamshala wherein as many as 40 persons has been converted from Part Time Casual Labourers into full time 
casual labourers as per the policy contained in Letter dated 25.08.2000 and 4..2000. I do find that infact claim of 
workman Parveen Kumar has been arbitrarily and illegally rejected for conversion into full time casual labourer 
from Part Time casual labourer . 


lI. From the evidence of Management witness Sh. Subhash Chand. It is clear that the witness in his cross 
examination has admitted that there were 63 posts in Dharamshala Circle and 40 post were filled up. From the 
perusal of various documents which has been brought on the record and proved by workman I am of the considered 
view that workman Parveen Kumar have been able to make out a case for conversion into full time casual labourer 
from part time casual labourer as per policies enshrined in letter dated 25.08.2000 and 4..2000. 


2. In the light of discussion made hereinabove and in the facts and circumstances of the present case the 
present reference No. L-400/2/202-IR(DU) dated 25.02.203 in respect of the action of the management i.e. 
General Manager Telecom, Shimla Circle in not converting the services of Sh. Parveen Kumar S/o Sh. Kisan Chand 
from part time safai karamchari to full time casual labour w.e.f. |7.05.2002 is held unjust, unfair and illegal. The 
reference stands adjudicated accordingly. Since the action of the Telecom Management Shimla Circle is held unjust, 
unfair and illegal, the workman Parveen Kumar is entitled for his conversion into full time casual labourer from part 
time casual labourer. 


3. It is therefore- 
ORDERED 


That the present ID No.l00/20I2 titled as Parveen Kumar Versus BSNL arising out of reference No. L- 
400/2/202-IR(DU) dated 25.02.20I3 is decided in favour of workman Parveen Kumar, the action of the 
management i.e. General Manager Telecom, Shimla Circle in not converting the services of Sh. Parveen Kumar S/o 
Sh. Kisan Chand from part time safai karamchari to full time casual labour w.e.f. 7.05.2002 is held unjust, unfair 
and illegal. The reference stands adjudicated accordingly. Since the action of the Telecom Management Shimla 
Circle is held unjust, unfair and illegal, the workman Parveen Kumar is entitled for his conversion into full time 
casual labourer from part time casual labourer. The BSNL Management is directed to convert workman Parveen

AWARD 


The Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L- 4202/3/20I5-IR(DU) dated 
0.6.20I5 referred the following dispute under section l0()(d) of the I.D. Act, 947 for adjudication to this 
Tribunal between the management of M/s. Indian Security Force and their workman. The reference is, 


“Whether the action of the management of M/s. Indian Security Force in terminating the services of Shri 
Ch.Yadaiah w.e.f. [3..204 is illegal, arbitrary and violation of Sec.25F of I.D. Act, 947? If yes, to 
what relief the workman is entitled to?” 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5887 


The reference is numbered in this Tribunal as I.D. No. 53/20I5 and notices were issued to the parties concerned. 
2. The averments made is the claim statement are as follows: 


It is submitted that the Petitioner was joined as House Keeping Supervisor (Semi skilled supervisor) in the 
Respondent company on .4.20, and was deputed as House Keeping supervisor in EFLU (English and Foreign 
Languages University), Tarnaka, Hyderbad. The duties assigned to him by the Respondent were as follows: for 
taking the attendance of about 290 workers, preparation of absentees list whenever required, updating all the leave 
balances and coordinating with the officials of EFLU in day to-day work. Petitioner discharged his duties to the 
satisfaction of the Respondent without any allegations and complaints neither from the side of the management nor 
from the side of the workers. At the time of joining in the Respondent company his salary was fixed as Rs.6,000/- 
per month, about fifteen months it was enhanced to Rs.8,000/-per month. On !6.9.204 Petitioner gave a letter to 
the Respondent with a request to enhance his salary from Rs.8,000/- to Rs.,000/-per month. It is submitted that 
without showing any valid reason on 2..20l4 at about 3.30 p.m the General Manager of the Respondent 
company namely P.S.Ramamurthy has orally informed the Petitioner to stop coming to duties from the next day 
onwards. On 3..204 to attend to his duty Petitioner has visited the office of the Respondent but he was 
stopped by the security at the entrance gate of the Respondent. Inspite of repeated requests the Respondent has 
not allowed the Petitioner from joining duties. | The above referred facts clearly reveals that the Respondent has 
acted as per their will and wish without following any procedure and not given any written termination letter and 
not given an opportunity the Petitioner to ask the reason for the illegal termination. It is submitted that 
Petitioner approached the Assistant Labor Commissioner (central)-!,Hyderabad. Then after the dispute was 
referred to this Hon’ble Court. After the illegal removal, the Respondent has given "Experience cum salary 
certificate" dated 26..204 stating that Petitioner had worked as a house keeping supervisor in EFLU, Tarnaka, 
Hyderabad. Further, stated that my performance was satisfactory and consolidated monthly salary is Rs.8,000/- 
per month. It is submitted that before the Assistant Labor Commissioner (Central)-l,Hyderabad the Respondent 
has filed reply vide their letter dated 29-l2-20i4 with false and baseless allegations, alleging that "he has 
misbehaved with some of the women workers and developed illegal intimacy with them with the result our 
organization is getting bad name. He has shown favoritism on some of the workers by manipulating their 
attendance in the registers. He is not telling to duties to his favorite workers and they are taking rest without doing 
proper duties. Some of the workers are leaving duties after signing in the attendance registers and they are leisurely 
attending on their duties" and also further alleged that Petitioner was simply sitting in the office room and 
spending time without supervision of the work and absenting from duties without any intimation and university 
authorities also unhappy. It is submitted that the above referred allegations are false and baseless. It is submitted 
that the Respondent has not followed Minimum Wages Act, therefore Petitioner approached the Regional Labour 
Commissioner(Central) at Hyderabad vide Application no.84/20i5. The said Regional Labour Commissioner(C) 
has directed the Respondent to pay a sum of Rs.38,674/- towards the difference amount as per the Central 
Minimum Wages Act and also imposed a sum of Rs.2000/- towards fine. The Respondent has paid the above 
referred amount through banker’s cheques dated 9.9.20I5. The Respondent also has not followed Bonus Act, 
Petitioner approached the Regional Labor commissioner(Central) at Hyderabad, who has directed the Respondent 
to pay a sum of Rs.l2,537/- towards the bonus, the said amount paid by the Respondent through banker’s cheque 
dated 9.9.20I5. Itis submitted that entire family consisting of two unemployed sons and _ wife have been 
depending on Petitioner’s income. It is submitted that the Respondent illegally terminated the Petitioner without 
any valid reason and without giving any prior notice or written notice and acted as per its will and wish without 
following any procedure and there is no fault of Petitioner. Therefore, prayed to reinstate the Petitioner as House 
Keeping supervisor in the Respondent company, with back wages from 3..20I4 to till reinstatement and 
Rs.50000/- towards compensation and costs of filing this case. 


3. Despite service of notice, Respondent did not file any counter in this case. Therefore, case was proceeded 
ex-parte against the Respondent vide order dated 5.2.209. 


4. In support of his claim petition Petitioner has filed chief statement of affidavit of himself as ४७। 
wherein he has reiterated the averments made in the claim petition. He has also filed the photocopies of nine 
documents in evidence vide list dated 3.0.20I5. The details of these documents are hereunder:- 5.४४] is the 
identity card issued by Respondent to the Petitioner. Ex.W2 is the letter dated 6.9.204 submitted by Petitioner to 
the Respondent to enhance his salary. Ex.W3 is the experience cum salary certificate issued by Respondent dated 
26..204. Ex.W4 is letter dated 29.2.20I4 filed by the Respondent before ALC(C)-l, Hyderabad. Ex.W5 is 
the reply/rejoinder letter dated 5..205 filed by the Petitioner before the ALC(C)-I, Hyderabad. Ex.W6 is the 
letter dated 7.3.20]5 filed by the Respondent before ALC(C)-l, Hyderabad. Ex.W7 & W8 are banker’s cheques 
dated 9.9.20I5 for Rs.38,674/- and Rs.2,000/- respectively issued by Respondent to the Petitioner. Ex.W9 is the 
Memorandum dated !6.4.205 stating that the minimum wages applicable to the workers w.e.f. .4.205 issued by 
Dy. CLC(C). 


5. Petitioner has alleged that he joined the service in the Respondent company on |.4.20ll as a House 
Keeping Supervisor (semi skilled supervisor) and his duties were, taking attendance of about 290 workers, 
preparation of absentees list whenever required, updating all the leave balance and coordinating with the officials 


5888 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


of EFLU in day to day work. Further, it is alleged that the Respondent without any valid reason or without issuing 
notice has illegally terminated the services of the Petitioner by oral order dated 2..204 with effect from 
30..20I4. Petitioner in his chief statement of affidavit states that from the day of his joining as supervisor in the 
Respondent company up to the date of illegal termination he has satisfactorily discharged his duties. After the 
illegal removal the Respondent has issued experience cum salary certificate dated 27..20l4 stating that the 
Petitioner has worked as a House Keeping Supervisor in EFLU, Tarnaka, Hyderabad and Petitioner was sincere 
and hardworking. It is further stated that his performance was satisfactory and his consolidated monthly salary 
was Rs.8000/- per month. 


6. The documentary evidence filed by the Petitioner are, Ex.W is the photocopy of the identity card which 
goes to show that Respondent company Indian Security Force issued identity card in the name of Petitioner with 
designation of supervisor. Further, Ex.W3 is experience cum salary certificate, showing that Petitioner had 
worked in the Respondent company as supervisor housekeeping. Further. Ex.W4 is the reply submitted by Indian 
Security Force, the Respondent to the ALC(C), ATI campus, Vidyanagar, Hyderabad wherein Respondent has 
admitted that the Petitioner was employee of the Respondent and they have stopped him from doing the job with 
effect from 2.!.204 and paid his salary through SBH, EFLU branch. Further, it is stated that the salary has 
been paid regularly and there are no dues to him. Further, it is stated that when Petitioner had joined the duty, 
Respondent used to pay Rs.6000/- per month upto June, 20l2 and later the Respondent enhanced the pay of 
Petitioner to Rs. 8000/- per month from July 20l2 to November 20l4. Thus, from the reply Ex.W4, submitted 
by Respondent company before ALC(C) it is established that Petitioner had worked in the employment of 
Respondent till November 20l4. As regards, rest of the allegations made by Respondent in his reply against 
Petitioner, are not established as Respondent did not appear and filed any reply or evidence in support of alleged 
charges. Undisputedly no departmental enquiry has been conducted by the Respondent against the Petitioner in 
this case. 


7. Therefore, in view of the above, it is established that the Petitioner had worked in Respondent company 
from i.e., .4.20I] to 2..204 without any interruption. Further, it is established that he has been terminated 
by the Respondent from service vide order dated !2..20l4, without giving one month statutory notice and 
without payment of any compensation amount as required under section 25 F of the I.D. Act, 947 for valid 
retrenchment of the Workman. Thus, Respondent has terminated Petitioner from his employment in contravention 
of the provision contained under section 25 F of the I.D. Act, 947. 


8. However, as regards the relief, prayed for reinstatement of Petitioner in the services of the Respondent 
company, the reference of the decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court is relevant, as discussed hereunder: - 


In the case of BSNL Vs. Bhurumal, Civil Appeal No.l0957/20I5 AIR 20i4 SUPREME COURT 488, 
Hon’ble Supreme Court have held:- 


“It would be, thus, seen that by a catena of decisions in recent time, this Court has clearly laid down that an 
order of retrenchment passed in violation of Section 25-F although may be set aside but an award of 
reinstatement should not, however, automatically passed. The award of reinstatement with full back wages in 
a case where the workman has completed 240 days of work in a year preceding the date of termination, 
particularly, daily wagers has not been found to be proper by this Court and instead compensation has been 
awarded. This Court has distinguished between a daily wager who does not hold a post and a permanent 
employee." Jagbir Singh has been applied very recently in Telegraph Deptt. V. Santosh Kumar ९६(/2॥, 
wherein this Court stated: (SCC p.777, para ll) "In view of the aforesaid legal position and the fact that the 
workmen were engaged as daily wagers about 25 years back and they worked hardly for 2 or 3 years, relief 
of reinstatement and back wages to them cannot be said to be justified and instead monetary compensation 
would subserve the ends of justice." 


23. It is clear from the reading of the aforesaid judgments that the ordinary principle of grant of 
reinstatement with full back wages, when the termination is found to be illegal is not applied mechanically in 
all cases. While that may be a position where services of a regular/permanent workman are terminated 
illegally and or malafide and/or by way of victimization, unfair labour practice etc. _ However, when it 
comes to the case of termination of a daily wage worker and where the termination is found illegal because 
of procedural defect, namely in violation of Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, this Court is 
consistent in taking the view in such cases reinstatement with back wages is not automatic and instead the 
workman should be given monetary compensation which will meet the ends of justice. Rationale for shifting 
in this direction is obvious.” 


In the case of Ashok Kumar Sharma Vs. Oberoi flight Services AIR 200 SCC page 502 wherein Hon’ble 
Supreme Court have held:- 


&. In the case of Sita Ram V. Moti Lal Nehru Farmers Training Institute2 this Court considered the matter 
thus: 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 5889 


727, The question, which, however, falls for our consideration is as to whether the Labour Court was 
justified in awarding reinstatement of the appellants in service. 


22. Keeping in view the period during which the services were rendered by the respondent (sic appellants); 
the fact that the respondent had stopped its operation of bee farming, and the services of the appellants were 
terminated in December /996, we are of the opinion that it is not a fit case where the appellants could have 
been directed to be reinstated in service. 


23. Indisputably, the Industrial Court, exercises a discretionary jurisdiction, but such discretion is required 
to be exercised judiciously. Relevant factors therefor were required to be taken into consideration; the 
nature of appointment, the period of appointment, the availability of the job, etc. should weigh with the court 
for determination of such an issue. 


24. This Court in a large number of decisions opined that payment of adequate amount of compensation in 

place of a direction to be reinstated in service in cases of this nature would subserve the ends of justice. (See 
Jaipur Development Authority v. Ramsahai [(2006) 77 SCC 684], M.P. Admn. v. Tribhuban [(2007) 9 SCC 
748] and Uttaranchal Forest Development Corpn. v. M.C. Joshi [(2007) 9 SCC 353]) 


25. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of this case, we are of the opinion that payment of a sum of 
Rs. 7,09,090 to each of the appellants, would meet the ends of justice. This appeal is allowed to the 
aforementioned extent. In the facts and circumstances of this case, there shall be no order as to costs." 


9. The afore-referred two decisions of this Court and few more decisions were considered by us in the case 
of Jagbir JT 2008 (3)SC622 Singh V. Haryana State Agriculture Marketing Board3 albeit in the context of 
retrenchment of a daily wager in violation of section 25F of Industrial Disputes Act who had worked for 
more than 240 days in a year and we observed thus: 


"7. It is true that earlier view of this Court articulated in many decisions reflected the legal position that if 
the termination of an employee was found to be illegal, the relief of reinstatement with full back wages would 
ordinarily follow. However, in recent past, there has been a shift in the legal position and in long line of 
cases, this Court has consistently taken the view that relief by way of reinstatement with back wages is not 
automatic and may be wholly inappropriate in a given fact situation even though the termination of an 
employee is in contravention to the prescribed procedure. Compensation instead of reinstatement has been 
held to meet the ends of justice." 


Therefore, in view of the fore gone discussion and law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court as discussed above, 
Petitioner in the present case is liable to get compensation from the Respondent in lieu of reinstatement in the 
employment. The present case is proceeding against the Respondent ex-parte and remained uncontroverted in the 
absence of any counter. Therefore, the claim petition of the Petitioner is liable to be allowed partly. 


9. In the present case at the hand, Petitioner has been terminated from service long back in the year 20/4. 
Therefore, in the facts and circumstances, it would be apposite to grant the relief of lumpsum compensation 
instead of his reinstatement into the employment of Respondent. As per claim of the Petitioner, he was getting 
Rs.8000/- per month salary at the time of termination. Therefore, a lumpsum compensation of Rs. 2,00,000/- 
would be appropriate relief in the present case. 


AWARD 


In view of the fore gone discussion, the action of the Respondent Indian Security Force, Hyderabad in 
terminating the services of the Petitioner Sri Ch. Yadaiah, w.e.f !2..204 is held illegal and unjustified as being 
in violation of provision of Sec.25F of the I.D. Act, 947. Therefore, the oral termination order dated 2..20I4 
of Petitioner from service is hereby set aside. Since Petitioner has been terminated from the service in the year 
204 and a long period has been elapsed since then, therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to get a compensation of 
Rs.2,00,000(Rupees Two Lakhs only) from Respondent for his illegal termination from service. Thus, 
Respondent is directed to pay the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- amount to the Petitioner within two months from 
receiving copy of this award, with all attendant benefits due to the Petitioner, failing which he has to pay the 
interest of 2% p.a.. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

received along with soft copy of the award by the Central Government on 23.07.2025.

The Commissioner, 


North Delhi Municipal Corporation, 


[भाग वा--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 589] 


4" Floor Civic Centre, Minto Road, 
New Delhi-!0002. 
Present: Sh. B.K Prasad, Ld. AR for the claimant. 
Sh. Arvind Kumar, Ld. AR for the management. 
Award 


l. In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour and 
Employment, vide its Order No. L-420/225/208-IR (DU) dated 3.02.20l9 has been pleased to refer the 
following dispute between the employer, that is the Management of North Delhi Municipal Corporation and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal, terms of which are as under: 


“Whether non-payment of wages by the management of North Delhi Municipal Corporation to Sh. Vikram 
Singh Rana S/o Sh. Harpal Singh Rana, Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 07.07.7994 in the pay scale of Rs. 950- 
4500/- revised from time to time attached to the said post with all consequential benefits upto 37.॥2.207, 
the date of superannuation as per direction of he Hon’ble High Court vide order dated 27.06, 2073 is illegal 
and unjustified? If so, what directions are necessary in this respect?” 


In pursuance to the reference, claimant had filed the claim statement stated that he has been employed on Muster 
Roll Mali on 2.05.982. Thereafter, he was initially appointed as regular Mali on 03.0i.985. He had been 
performing the duty of an Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 till his superannuation up to 3l.2.20I7 under Rohini 
Zone (Horticulture) under North Delhi Municipal Corporation. Management has fixed the different pay scales to 
their employees including Mali, Chaudhary etc. in accordance to their job profile. He was not given the grant of 
proper pay scale of officiating Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0i.994 to 3.2.20l7 which amount to force labour and the 
management is indulging in unfair labour practice. He had got the payment in lower pay scale of Mali Rs. 750-940/- 
revised from time to time and he has been denied the pay scale of Rs. 950-500/- for his duty performed as 
Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 revised from time to time. He had stated that Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in the matter 
of Jai Chand vs. MCD (CW No. 654/200) has disapproved the non-payment vide order dated 02.05.2003 for the 
post of Chaudhary. The same stand has been taken by the Hon’ble Division Bench of High Court of Delhi in the 
matter of MCD vs. Sultan Singh & Ors. in W.P. (C) No. 7947/200. As such, he claims that he may be awarded 
the payment of Acting Chaudhary in the pay scale of Rs. 950-l500/- revised from time to time to him w.e.f. 
0I.0.994 up to his superannuation. 


2. Respondent herein has filed the ४४.७. stating that the claimant does not disclose the correct facts and has filed the 
claim without any locus. Workman is not eligible for any kind of relief as prayed by him in the present application 
and the said application is nothing but an abuse of process of law and waste of precious judicial time. It has been 
submitted by him that workman was promoted as a Chaudhary in September, 204 and on his retirement he had 
already received all the consequential benefit of his retirement. He submitted that there is no such provision in the 
tules of the respondent management of giving benefits of acting Chaudhary to the claimant because it is merely a 
change of work and administrative arrangement and not a promotion. He further submitted that workman is trying to 
misguide the court by showing the internal office record of the management whereas he has no such authority to use 
the official documents of the management, the same being for internal use of the management. He had denied that 
the management has fixed any pay scale for officiating Chaudhary. However, he had admitted that there are different 
pay scales for different posts. He further denied that Mali and Chawkidar who are performing their duty as Acting 
Chaudhary were granted the pay scale of Chaudhary. He submitted that claim petition be dismissed. 


3. After completion of pleadings vide order dated 4.08.209, following issues had been framed: 


a. Whether the NDMC illegally refused to grant the revised pay scale to the workman w.e.f. 0.0.94 in the post of 
acting Choudhary. 


b. Whether the management illegally denied such revised pay scale to the workman upto 3!.2.20I7 the date of his 
superannuation ignoring the direction of the Hon’ble High Court vide order dated 27.08.203. 


c. To what relief the claimant is entitled to. 


4. In order to prove its claim, the workman himself had entered into the witness box. He deposed the fact that he was 
allotted the work of an Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 and performed his duty under Rohini Zone 
(Horticulture) till his superannuation up to 3!..20l7. His name has been appearing at Serial No. 25 in the list of 
officiating Chaudhary issued by the Dy. Director (Horticulture) West Zone which is Exhibit १४७१/॥. He submitted 
that he is entitled to the wages of Acting Chaudhary in the pay scale of Rs. 950-500 revised from time to time w.e-f. 
0I.0.994 up to 3.2.207 along with all consequential benefits. 


5. Witness was put to the cross-examination where he admitted that he had never lodged any complaint in the office 
of the management claiming his unpaid dues which is the subject matter of the present proceeding since he was told 


5892 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


that his matter shall be taken up by the management with the case of similarly placed person. In the year 204 he has 
got the promotion to the post of supervisor from the post of Mali. He had filed the document which has been marked 
as Ex. १४५७४|/।. This document was given to him by the management and he did not have the original. He had denied 
that the claim has been filed on the basis of false and fabricated document. 


6. In rebuttal, one Sh. Rakesh Kumar, Assitant Director (Horticulture), Rohini Zone, MCD has been examined by 
the counsel of the management, wherein he had reiterated the facts and mentioned by him in the W.S. He had 
admitted that initially he had joined the MCD at the post of Maali. Thereafter, he was promoted to the post of 
Assistant Director in January, 2024. He admitted that Ex. ४ै/७४॥/|, the list of workmen including the workman in 
question who had been shown at Serial No. 25 as Acting Chaudhary. He stated that the list pertain to the west zone. 
West Zone was bifurcated and one of the zone was known as Rohini Zone. 


7. Ihave heard the argument at par, perused the record and analyzed the evidence. The whole of the case of the 
claimant rest upon the fact that management witness has admitted the list Ex. ४४/५७॥/| wherein name of the workman 
had been shown at S.No. 25. He was 0" pass, appointed as “Mali” on 03.0.985 and looking after the work of 
Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0!.0!.994. He had made prayer that considering the above facts on record and in view of 
the judgment passed by the Hon’ble High Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Sultan Singh & 
others W.P. (C) No. 7947 of 200, decided on 20.04.20ll where similarly placed person had been given the higher 
scale so he be given the pay scale of Acting Chaudhary revised from time to time. 


8. While the respondent stand is that the workman’s service was earlier regularized as Mali in [985 and he was 
promoted in the year September, 204 and till then he has been paid all the benefit of the Acting Chaudhary. He was 
retired in the year 207 and he had been paid all the benefits therein. He further submits that workman is not entitled 
to the benefit for the pay scale of the Acting Chaudhary. 


9. Here, it is not disputed that the claimant has not been working as Acting Chaudhary since 994. MW himself 
admitted the list issued by management where the name of the claimant has been shown as I0" pass and has been 
working as an Acting Chaudhary since 994. Operating portion of the judgment of Sultan Singh & Others in which 
the workman has placed reliance, where in para no. 28, it was observed: 


“28. Considering the entire facts and circumstances it is apparent that the claim of the respondents have 
always been that they should be paid the difference in pay of Mali/Chowkidar and the Garden Chaudhary 
as they were made to work on the post of Garden Chaudhary whereas the petitioner had first denied that 
they worked as Garden Chaudharies, then took the plea that the Assistant Director (Horticulture) was not 
competent to ask the respondents to work as Garden Chaudharies and that the respondents cannot be 
appointed to the post of Garden Chaudharies in accordance with the recruitment rules. There is no doubt 
that respondents are not claiming appointment to the post of Garden Chaudharies on account of having 
worked on ad-hoc basis on the post of Garden Chaudhary contrary to rules or that some of them not 
having the requisite qualifications are entitled for relaxation.” 


0. It is not out of place mention here that even if the claimant herein was not a party in Sultan’s case referred 
above, judgment of Hon’ble High Court is binding on the management and the management is required to implement 
the same. When the workman had been assigned the job of an ‘Acting Chaudhary’ i.e. a higher post then that of 
‘Mali’ for so long (for the last 20 years), he should have been designated as Acting Chaudhary. However, if that was 
not done, then he would also be entitled for the pay scale of an Acting Chaudhary instead of Mali. 


ll. In the light of above discussion, issue no. | decided against the management and in favour of the workman. 
Issue no. 2 is also decided against the management and in favour of the workman. 


2. In view of the above, workman/claimant is entitled to the pay scale of Acting Chaudhary since 994 to 204, 
when he was actually promoted to the post. Respondent herein is liable to pay the difference of the wages of Mali 
and Acting Chaudhary from the date, when the workman herein was performing duty till he was actually promoted, 
management is directed to pay the entire difference of the salary within two months from the date of passing the 
award. Award is passed accordingly. A copy of this award is sent to the appropriate government for notification as 
required under section I7 of the I.D Act, 947. 


ATUL KUMAR GARG, Presiding officer

Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947) (“the Act” in short), the Central Government has referred the industrial 
dispute between the employers, in relation to the management of Axis Bank and one other and their union 
Maharashtra Sanghathit Asanghathit Kamgar Sabha(HMS) for adjudication, as per letter No.NGP/8(03)/2025-ID 
(RLCNGP) dated 28.05.2025, with the following schedule:- 


“Whether the action of the contractor M/s. Seven-s Banking management consultancy services (P) 
Itd. And the management of Axis Bank Ltd., Mumbai through its managing director in not 
transferring the workman namely Shubham Tavide, Sagar Godkale, not granting advance to 
Rajendra Sonawane and Kamalakar Shinde and not posting the activists of other unions as 
supervisors are legal and justified? If not, to what relief the union i.e. Maharashtra Sanghatit and 
Asanghatit Kamgar sabha is entitled to?” 


2. On receipt of the reference, notices were issued to the parties i.e. the union “Maharashtra Sanghatit and 
Asanghatit Kamgar sabha”, (“the union” in short) and the management of M/s. Seven-s Banking consultancy 
services (P) Ltd., and M/s. Axis Bank Ltds, (“party no.l” in short). Today is the |“ date of the case in which the 
petitioners has to file their statement of claim, but instead of statement of claim one Shri Suryakant Bagal appeared 
before the court and file an application mentioning that the workman therein the reference i.e. Shri Shubham 
Tavide and Rejendra Sonawane have left the Axis Bank and the grievances of the remaining workman i.e. Shri 
Sagar Godkale and Kamalakar Shinde are resolved. Hence the above reference does not exist and requested to 
close the matter. 

As the petitioner union requested to close the reference an award is passed against the petitioner. 

Hence, it is ordered:- 

ORDER 

“The action of the contractor M/s. Seven-s Banking management consultancy services (P) Itd. And 
the management of Axis Bank Ltd., Mumbai through its managing director in not transferring the 
workman namely Shubham Tavide, Sagar Godkale, not granting advance to Rajendra Sonawane and 
Kamalakar Shinde and not posting the activists of other unions as supervisors are legal and justified. The 
union is not entitled to any relief.

S.O. 559.—In pursuance of Section 7 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947), the Central 
Government hereby publishes the Award (Ref. No. 26/200) of the Central Government Industrial Tribunal- 
cum-Labour Court, Asansol as shown in the Annexure, in the industrial dispute between the Management of 
ECL and their workmen received by the Central Government on /08/2025. 

[No. L-2202/38/2000 - IR (CM-ID] 


SALONI, Dy. Director 


ANNEXURE 
BEFORE THE CENTRAL GOVT. INDUSTRIAL TRIBUNAL -CUM- LABOUR COURT, 
ASANSOL. 
PRESENT: Shri Ananda Kumar Mukherjee, 


Presiding Officer, 
C.G.LT-cum-L.C., Asansol. 
REFERENCE CASE NO. 26 OF 200] 


PARTIES: Rajkumar Singh 
Vs. 

Management of Madhabpur Colliery, ECL 
REPRESENTATIVES: 
For the Union/Workman: Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress. 
For the Management of ECL: Mr. P. K. Das, Advocate. 
INDUSTRY: Coal. 
STATE: West Bengal. 
Dated: 8.06.2025 


AWARD 


In exercise of power conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section () and Sub-section (2A) of Section l0 of 
the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
Order No. L-2202/38/2000-IR(C-ID dated 02.08.200I has been pleased to refer the following dispute between 
the employer, that is the Management of Madhabpur Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“ Whether the action of the management of Madhavpur Colliery of M/s. ECL in dismissing Sh. Rajkumar 
Singh, Pit Clerk from services w.e.f. /3.3.93 is legal and justified? If not, to what relief the workman is 
entitled to ? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/38/2000-IR(C-ID) dated 02.08.200l from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0.09.200I/ 
9..200] and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to 
appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2; Mr. Rakesh Kumar, the then General Secretary of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on 
20.02.2002 on behalf of Rajkumar Singh, the dismissed workman of Madhabpur Colliery under Kajora Area of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). In brief, the fact of the case disclosed in the written 
statement of the union is that Rajkumar Singh was a permanent employee of ECL and was working as an 
Attendance Clerk at Madhabpur Colliery. On 5.05.!993 he was dismissed from his service without observing 
necessary formalities as per standing orders of the company and without holding any enquiry. Further case of the 
union is that on 4.05.993 an incident took place in connection with which he was charged by the management 


594 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


but no Charge Sheet was issued and without holding any domestic enquiry the workman was dismissed form his 
service on the basis of a prima facie enquiry. No second Show Cause Notice was issued to the workman which is a 
mandatory requirement as per a decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. It is contended that Rajkumar 
Singh has no involvement in the case for which he was dismissed and urged that the order of dismissal issued 
against him is illegal and the same is liable to be set aside. Union has prayed for re-instatement of the workman 
with full back wages. 


3; Management initially did not file any written statement and the case was fixed up for ex-parte hearing. 
Thereafter management filed written statement on 25.03.2003. According to the management of ECL, Rajkumar 
Singh while on duty had taken a Dumper bearing No. WB39-I50] loaded with eight tons of coal from Madhabpur 
Colliery and he himself drove the Dumper towards the railway crossing of Kajoragram where he was caught by the 
security guard of railway site. For the aforesaid act of misconduct Rajkumar Singh was chargesheeted by the 
management under Clause |7(i)(a), !7(i)G) and 7(i)(q) of the Model Standing Orders applicable to the Mine. The 
workman submitted reply to the Charge Sheet but as the reply was not satisfactory a domestic enquiry was ordered 
against him and the Enquiry Officer held the enquiry in which the workman participated. Reasonable opportunity 
was given to the workman to defend himself. The Enquiry Officer observed the principles of natural justice and 
after concluding the enquiry proceeding submitted his report before the Appointing Authority. The charge of 
misconduct was duly proved against Rajkumar Singh. After careful consideration of the Charge Sheet, Enquiry 
Proceeding, Enquiry Report and other connected papers, the Disciplinary Authority dismissed the workman 
from service. Management contended that the contents of paragraph no. 3 of the written statement filed by the 
union is incorrect and that the workman was not dismissed without holding any enquiry. Management denied that 
the workman was dismissed from service without service of Charge Sheet and without holding any domestic 
enquiry. According to the management dismissal of the workman is totally justified and the workman is not 
entitled to any relief. 


4. Rajkumar Singh has been examined as Workman Witness No. |. He has filed affidavit-in-chief wherein 
he stated that on 4.05.993 he was on duty in the second shift from 04.00 PM to 2.00 AM at Madhabpur 
Colliery. After completing his duty, he was proceeding towards his quarters at Khas Kajora Colliery, Madhabpur 
Railway siding on the way to his quarter at Khas Kajora Colliery. At about !2 at night when he reached the 
Railway Crossing at Kajoragram he saw a Dumper was intercepted. He was held up at that place without knowing 
the fact and was handed over to the police and subsequently forwarded to the Jail. It is contended that the 
management did not take any action against the driver who was on duty and drove the Dumper, leaving it at the 
Railway Crossing. Further case of the workman is that the management decided to dismiss him on the same date 
ie., on 5.05.993 without holding any enquiry and without giving him any opportunity to defend his case before 
the Enquiry Officer. The dismissed workman contended that management dismissed him from service on the basis 
of prejudice and no second Show Cause Notice was issued to him as per guidelines issued by the Coal India 
Limited. The workman averred that the order of dismissal passed against him is illegal and unjustified. 


5. Management cross-examined the witness where he deposed that Police lodged an FIR against him and 
submitted Charge Sheet after investigation and the case is pending before the Court at Durgapur. Witness further 
deposed that since he was in custody he never appeared in any Domestic Enquiry. It transpires from the evidence 
that he received Charge Sheet from the management through the Jail Authority and after his release from jail he 
submitted an application before the management regarding non-supply of Charge Sheet and other documents. 
Witness denied that he has been rightly dismissed by the management and volunteered that he was dismissed while 
he was in custody. 

6. From the record as well as order dated 02.07.20l3 it appears that management did not adduce any 
evidence in this case after several opportunity granted to them. On the date of hearing of argument, the order of 
dismissal dated 5.05.!993 has been admitted by both parties and marked as Exhibit ४-।. 


7. The moot question in this case is whether the dismissal of workman from service under ECL is 
sustainable under the law. If not, what relief the workman is entitled to? 

8. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Union representative argued that the workman has been dismissed form service 
without holding any enquiry. The allegation against him was theft of 8 tonnes of coal, taken away by the workman 
with the help of a Dumper on 4.05.993. The workman was arrested and was kept in jail custody for about a 
month till he was released on bail. The management without issuing any Charge Sheet and without holding any 
enquiry against him dismissed him from service on the very next date vide order dated 5.05.993 (Exhibit W-). 
The union representative urged that such act of dismissal of workman is arbitrary, violative of the principles of 
natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside. 

9. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL admitted that the management is unable to 
produce any Charge Sheet or Enquiry Proceeding on the basis on which the order of dismissal was passed by the 
General Manager. It is submitted that the workman committed theft in respect of the employer’s property and he 
was found guilty of the charge under Clause !7(i)(a) of Model Standing Orders. It is argued that the workman is 
not entitled to any relief in this case as he has committed a criminal offence. 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 595 


0. I have considered the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by the union 
representative and learned advocate of the management. It is undisputed that Rajkumar Singh was working as 
Attendance Clerk at Madhabpur Colliery and he was dismissed from his service by order dated 5.05.993, issued 
by the General Manager, Kajora Area bearing No. KA:PM:C-6:0/387/288, in which he has stated that Rajkumar 
Singh had allegedly taken Dumper No. WB39-50] loaded with 8 tonnes of coal from Pit No. 2 of Madhabpur 
Colliery and drove towards the Railway Crossing of Kajoragram and that he was caught with the Dumper by 
Security Guard Mr. Rajdeo Ahir and Md. Daud Khan of Madhabpur Colliery who were on duty at Madhabpur 
Colliery Siding. On receipt to the report, the Agent, Madhabpur Colliery appointed an Enquiry Officer to conduct 
the enquiry into the alleged misconduct. It is further stated in the order of dismissal that the enquiry was conducted 
in presence of Rajkumar Singh and statements were recorded. The Enquiry Officer thereafter submitted his report 
and after going through the Enquiry Report it was found that Rajkumar Singh committed the misconduct under 
Clause 7(i)(a), [7@)(@) and 7(i)(q) of the Model Standing Orders applicable to the company. It is further stated 
that after careful consideration of the report of the Enquiry Officer, connected papers and gravity of misconduct, 
the General Manager dismissed the workman. No Charge Sheet, Enquiry Proceeding has been produced by the 
management to establish that a proper enquiry proceeding was held before the workman was found guilty of the 
charge. There is no iota of evidence to indicate that the workman had opportunity to represent his case. Under such 
facts and circumstances, I hold that the dismissal of Rajkumar Singh on the strength of letter KA:PM:C- 
6:0/387/288 dated 5.05.993, issued by the General Manager, Kajora Area is arbitrary and found unsustainable 
under the law and in violation of principles of natural justice. The workman having been dismissed in an illegal 
manner is entitled to be reinstated. It is appropriate to set aside the order of dismissal dated 5.05.993. The 
workman is entitled to be reinstated in service within two (2) months from the date of communication of the 
Award, if has not attained the age of superannuation till date. It transpires from the materials in record and 
admission of the workman that he was in jail custody and a criminal case is pending against him. The workman has 
not rendered service to the employer company since !5.05.993. Therefore, I am not inclined to grant him full 
back wages for the period he remained idle. It is found appropriate to grant him twenty percent (20%) of his back 
wages from [5.05.993 till his reinstatement in service or superannuation, whichever is earlier. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Madhabpur Colliery under 
Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The order of dismissal of Rajkumar Singh, Pit Clerk of Madhabpur 
Colliery is set aside. Management of ECL is directed to reinstate the workman within two (2) months from the date 
of communication of the Award, if the workman has not attained the age of superannuation in the meantime. The 
management shall also pay back wages to the workman at the rate of twenty percent (20%) from 5.05.993 till his 
reinstatement or superannuation whichever is earlier. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let 
copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India, New Delhi for information and 
Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERJEE, Presiding Officer

AWARD. 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub —section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947),Government Of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No.L-2002/57/2004-IR(C-I) dated 28/06/2004 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer i.e. management of Bastacolla Area of M/s. BCCL and their workman through Secretary, Bihar Colliery 
Kamgar Union, Hirapur, Dhanbad for adjudication by this Tribunal: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of Kuya Colliery of M/s BCCL, Bastacolla Area, P.O.-Jharia, 
Distt. Dhanbad in not providing employment to Smt. Ladi Rajwarin. Wife of late Dasrath Rajwar, Pump 
Khalasi, P.No. 09863 as per the provision of N.C.W.A. is proper and justified? If not, to what relief is the 
said dependent wife of the deceased workman entitled?” 


2. On receiving order no. L-2002/57/2004-IR(C-D dated 28/06/2004 Government of India, Ministry of Labour, 
New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, Reference case no. 60 of 2004 was registered on !2.07.2004 and 
thereafter the notices were sent to the parties with a direction to appear and submit their written statements along 
with relevant documents in support of their claims and the witnesses. 


3. After issuance of regd. notice, written statement has been filed by Sri K. Chakraborty, Ld. Advocate on 
behalf of the workman. Sri U.N. Lal, Ld. Advocate appeared from the side of the management and filed his letter 
of authority on !7.02.2005. It further transpires that written statement and rejoinder has been filed by the 
management but when the case record was put up after a long gap, registered notices were again sent but neither 
the workman nor the management appeared before this Tribunal, though on 20.06.2025, Sri Rishi Raj Meena, 
Asstt. Manager (Legal) for the management appeared. 


4. On perusal of the entire case record it is transpires that the workman never appeared before this Tribunal from 
5.02.2006, which shows that the workman has lost his interest in this case and therefore, for the ends of justice, 
this case deserves to be dismissed for non prosecution. 


5. Hence, 
ORDERED 


that this case is hereby dismissed and a “No Dispute Award” be drawn up in respect of the above reference case. 
Let the copies of Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, New 
Delhi for information and notification. 


SACHINDRA KUMAR PANDEY, Presiding Officer

“Whether the action of the Management of Argada Area of M/s CCL in denying regularization as 
Time Rated Category-l worker to Smt. Samarji Devi, piece rated worker, is justified and legal? If

Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, Reference case no. 27 of 2007 was registered on 03.07.2007 
and thereafter the notices were sent to the parties with a direction to appear and submit their written statements 
along with relevant documents in support of their claims and the witnesses.

regd. notices were issued to both parties on 06.0i.2022 but even then no one appeared. Thereafter again regd.
